label: Positions & Commitments
short: Philosophical, political, economic, and institutional commitments.
title: What must powerful systems preserve?
body: Boundary First Labs takes explicit but revisable positions on the design of consequential systems. Philosophically, representations participate in what systems can perceive, preserve, decide, and repair. Politically, people who bear material consequences require meaningful representation, contestability, and recourse. Economically, throughput and ownership are insufficient measures of welfare: access, capacity, risk, externality, utilization, and repair also matter. Institutionally, authority, evidence, responsibility, consequence, memory, and repair must remain coupled rather than being distributed until no one can answer for failure.
takeaways: One method. One living system. Many boundaries to repair.
Our roots must balance our branches.
No consequence without representation.
Responsibility must land.
Repair is infrastructure.
No hidden human shock absorbers.
No undeclared “we.”
Throughput is not identical to welfare.
Contestability and repair are system requirements.
Knowledge should become public through responsible stewardship, not fragmentation or indiscriminate release.
Finance is the law of who may borrow from the future.
No orphan assets. No unfunded delegation.
A market value gain does not erase a loss of household, ecological, or institutional closure.
Criticism is part of public repair.
claims: Every representation preserves some relations and suppresses others.
People who bear a system's consequences require standing within its processes of decision, contest, and repair.
Economic systems should be judged by how value, access, capacity, risk, and consequence move through them.
Institutions fail when authority, evidence, responsibility, consequence, and repair become structurally separated.
Knowledge publication is itself a consequential system design problem when context, capability, interpretation, and repair are unevenly distributed.
Public commitments should be expressible not only in institutional prose but in forms that ordinary audiences can question, remember, repeat, and contest.
Markets, law, finance, labor, ecology, and infrastructure are institutional systems whose boundaries determine which costs, voices, and future obligations become visible.
Creditworthiness is not identical to system-worthiness: an obligation may be repayable while still degrading the capacities required to sustain the larger system.
Public trust requires that delegated power, public consequence, lifecycle obligation, and repair authority remain representable and contestable.
coreThesis: Consequential systems should preserve human standing, meaningful participation, accountable power, durable capacity, and viable paths to repair.

positionFamilies.title: Philosophical Position: Representation Is Consequential
positionFamilies.thesis: People and institutions act through distinctions, categories, models, measurements, interfaces, laws, and narratives. These representations do not merely describe a system; they shape what the system can perceive, preserve, decide, and repair.
commitments: Every representation preserves some relations and suppresses others.
Omission becomes consequential when action is based on the representation.
Boundaries can enable coherent action without erasing what lies beyond them.
Models, institutions, and doctrines must remain revisable when defects become visible.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Philosophical and methodological position; domain claims require domain evidence.

positionFamilies.title: Political Position: No Consequence Without Representation
positionFamilies.thesis: People who bear the material consequences of a system require meaningful standing in the processes by which it is authorized, evaluated, contested, and repaired.
commitments: Representation requires access to reasons, not only symbolic consultation.
Standing should track exposure to consequence.
Appeal must be capable of changing an outcome or repairing harm.
Power remains legitimate only while the agency conditions authorizing it remain meaningfully preserved.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Laboratory doctrine and political philosophy, not a claim that one procedure fits every jurisdiction.

positionFamilies.title: Economic Position: Capacity, Access, and Consequence Belong in the Ledger
positionFamilies.thesis: An economy should be evaluated not only by aggregate throughput or price, but by how value, access, productive capacity, risk, maintenance, dependency, and consequence move through the system.
commitments: Throughput is not identical to welfare.
Ownership is not identical to productive use.
Externalized costs are failures of representation and accounting.
Household continuity, labor agency, and underused capacity are legitimate economic design concerns.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Applied economic framework requiring empirical and legal grounding before policy use.

positionFamilies.title: Institutional Position: Authority Must Remain Traceable and Repairable
positionFamilies.thesis: Institutions are systems for transporting facts, authority, memory, legitimacy, responsibility, and consequence across people and time.
commitments: Authority without accountability becomes sovereignty by insulation.
Procedure must remain connected to purpose and affected reality.
Institutional memory, provenance, contestability, and repair are core infrastructure.
Responsibility must include the authority and resources required to repair failure.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Institutional design doctrine requiring case-specific implementation.

positionFamilies.title: Epistemic Position: Public Knowledge Requires Correction Mechanisms
positionFamilies.thesis: Science, journalism, education, courts, archives, adversarial review, and civic inquiry are not ornamental institutions. They are mechanisms by which public representations can be challenged and corrected.
commitments: Claims should expose their sources, maturity, limits, and alternatives.
Criticism is a maintenance function rather than a betrayal of institutional loyalty.
No expert body should become a hidden priesthood of unchallengeable boundary definers.
Public reason requires plural evidence channels and durable correction paths.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Public philosophy and institutional doctrine; factual claims require source support.

positionFamilies.title: Technological Position: Capability Must Remain Bounded by Human Purpose
positionFamilies.thesis: Technology should enlarge meaningful human capacity without becoming a consequence sink, self-authorizing sovereign, or mechanism for making affected people illegible.
commitments: The lab is pro-progress rather than anti-technology.
Capability is incomplete without authorization, legibility, contestability, attribution, and repair.
Some boundary violations should be prohibited rather than optimized or normalized.
AI inherits and scales the boundary discipline of its deployment context.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Normative technology doctrine and research thesis; particular safety claims require evidence.

positionFamilies.title: Ecological Position: Material Substrate Remains Binding
positionFamilies.thesis: Energy, water, land, materials, climate, biological systems, and human bodies remain part of the real operating domain even when economic or technical representations exclude them.
commitments: Ecological and material costs must not disappear behind price, abstraction, or organizational boundaries.
Maintenance and replacement obligations belong inside project design.
A system that consumes its substrate faster than it can restore or replace it is not durably closed.
Future agents deserve representation in decisions that irreversibly narrow their options.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Cross-cutting design position requiring domain science and lifecycle data.

positionFamilies.title: Civilizational Position: Growing Power Requires Growing Consequence Literacy
positionFamilies.thesis: Civilizations become vulnerable when agency amplifiers couple social, technical, economic, political, ecological, and epistemic systems faster than institutions can represent and repair their connected consequences.
commitments: Our roots must balance our branches.
Governance is a survival technology when it preserves the conditions of future agency.
Progress should be judged partly by repair capacity, not only by expansion or speed.
Civilization-scale claims remain hypotheses and diagnostic frames until supported by comparative evidence.
positionFamilies.claimCeiling: Civilizational systems hypothesis, not a solved theory of history or the Great Filter.

publicCovenant: Boundary First Labs builds tools, methods, products, institutions, and public arguments that make hidden system boundaries visible, teachable, measurable, governable, and repairable. One method. One living system. Many boundaries to repair. We are pro-progress: human capability should grow, but our roots must balance our branches. No consequence without representation. Responsibility must land. Repair is infrastructure. Systems should not hide failure inside unrecognized human burden, and collective claims should not invoke an undeclared “we.” Power must remain coupled to consequence, institutions must remain accountable to those for whom they are responsible, and no consequential system should erase the people, conditions, substrates, or future options on which it depends.

history.orientation: The public positions combine humanist, republican, pragmatic, systems, ecological, and institutional traditions. They are not a party platform. They are a doctrine of how growing power should remain answerable to affected people, material conditions, and future repair.

historicalArc.development: Ethics and politics were framed around human flourishing, civic responsibility, practical judgment, and the organization of common life.

historicalArc.period: Early modern constitutionalism and political economy
historicalArc.development: Theories of rights, representation, divided authority, markets, and public legitimacy developed alongside modern states and commercial systems.

historicalArc.period: Twentieth-century pragmatism, systems thought, and ecology
historicalArc.development: Attention shifted toward consequences, feedback, institutions, interdependence, ecological limits, and the conditions under which complex systems remain viable.

buildsFrom.author: Aristotle
buildsFrom.relation: Background for practical judgment, flourishing, civic organization, and the relation between individual and common good.

buildsFrom.author: John Dewey
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for defining publics through shared consequences and for treating democratic institutions as instruments of collective inquiry.

buildsFrom.author: Amartya Sen
buildsFrom.relation: A modern lineage for evaluating institutions by substantive human capabilities rather than output alone.

buildsFrom.author: Donella H. Meadows
buildsFrom.relation: A systems lineage for feedback, leverage, delayed consequence, and the conditions of durable intervention.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The lab condensed its public doctrine into the propositions “No consequence without representation” and “Our roots must balance our branches.”
Economic, institutional, technological, and ecological positions were organized around representation, standing, responsibility, substrate, and repair.
Constructive Humanist Agentics supplied the normative test for delegated agency, while civilization-scale work extended the same commitments across longer timescales and larger coupled systems.
aimsToward: A pro-progress public philosophy in which capability and accountability rise together.
Political and economic systems that preserve meaningful standing for those who bear their consequences.
A civilizational ethic capable of representing future agency, ecological substrate, and the maintenance conditions of progress.

label: Constructive Humanist Agentics
short: Capability that enlarges human capacity without erasing responsibility.
title: Agency must remain humanly answerable.
body: Constructive Humanist Agentics is the design and governance of delegated agency so that growing capability enlarges human capacity while remaining bounded by representation, consequence, contestability, responsibility, and repair. It is constructive because it builds capabilities, institutions, tools, and repair paths rather than relying only on prohibition. It is humanist because operational capability does not confer legitimacy, sovereignty, or self-authorization. It is agentic because it studies systems that select, execute, or shape consequential transitions under delegated authority.
takeaways: An agent may extend human power, but not become where human responsibility disappears.
No agent may grant itself the authority under which it acts.
Greater capability requires stronger coupling between power and consequence.
No responsibility without the capacity to repair.
Human control is meaningful only when interfaces fit the perception, cognition, embodiment, language, and practical capacity of the people expected to use or contest them.
claims: Operational capability does not by itself confer legitimacy or sovereignty.
Affected people must remain visible as agents rather than being reduced to variables, users, or targets.
Agentic systems should remain authorized, bounded, legible, contestable, attributable, and repairable.
Accessibility and human factors are conditions of standing and agency, not merely interface polish.

documents.title: Constructive Humanist Agentics: Cycle, Pressure, and Grammar

coreThesis: Delegated agency should enlarge human capacity while preserving human standing, accountable authority, consequence traceability, contestability, and repair.

humanFactorsInterface.principle: A system cannot claim to preserve human agency when its controls, explanations, appeals, or repair paths are unusable by the people who depend on them.

agencyDoctrine.constitutionalProposition: An agentic system may extend human power, but it may not become the place where human responsibility disappears.
humanAgencyConditions: retain intelligible options for future action

agenticSystemTests.question: Who granted the system authority, for what purpose, and under what revocation conditions?
What may the system change, and what must it preserve?
Can responsible and affected people understand the operative action, evidence, limits, and consequence path?
Can an affected person challenge, refuse, appeal, interrupt, or seek correction?
Can consequential action terminate in identifiable human or legal stewardship?
Who can halt, reverse, compensate, correct, retrain, redesign, or retire the system?
Would you put your family inside this system?

delegationRules: Authority remains derivative from accountable people and institutions.
No system may expand the conditions authorizing its own agency without separate authorization and review.
Responsibility cannot be assigned without corresponding repair capacity.
Standing should follow exposure to consequence, including indirect and cumulative consequence.
Exit is not an adequate substitute for due process where a system is essential, unavoidable, or monopolistic.
Human oversight is meaningful only when humans retain information, time, authority, and practical ability to intervene.
Some boundary violations should be prohibited rather than accepted as ordinary performance tradeoffs.
agencyClasses: infrastructure and market systems that shape reachable action

programs.title: Public Agency Map
programs.description: Maps who may act, who authorized action, whose options are expanded or constrained, where consequence lands, who may contest, and who can repair.
programs.claimCeiling: Diagnostic method requiring case evidence and affected-party review.

programs.title: Agency Audit
programs.description: Assesses authorization, boundaries, affected agency, contestability, attribution, repair, and self-expansion risk in consequential AI, software, and institutional systems.
programs.claimCeiling: Assessment and governance instrument, not universal certification by itself.

programs.title: Agentic Closure Certification
programs.description: Explores whether consequential artificial agency can be certified against declared authority, invariants, escalation conditions, consequence ownership, and repair paths.
programs.claimCeiling: Proposed certification architecture requiring standards comparison, pilots, and independent governance.

programs.title: AI Non-Aggression and Hard Boundary Doctrine
programs.description: Identifies classes of artificial action that should be forbidden rather than optimized, normalized, or merely disclosed.
programs.claimCeiling: Normative proposal requiring precise definitions, legal analysis, and domain-specific evidence.

programs.title: Artificial Sovereignty and Self-Authorization
programs.description: Studies when platforms, corporations, institutions, or artificial systems become functionally sovereign by controlling essential interfaces while escaping meaningful contestability and responsibility.
programs.claimCeiling: Analytic concept; claims about specific entities require evidence and legal care.

programs.title: Affected-Agent Standing
programs.description: Develops the principle that standing, notice, explanation, and repair rights should track material exposure to consequence rather than only ownership, contract, or direct transaction.
programs.claimCeiling: Normative and legal-design proposal requiring jurisdictional development.

programs.title: Embodied and Accessible Agency
programs.description: Treats cognition, disability, embodiment, time, attention, language, interface complexity, and practical control as conditions of real rather than nominal agency.
programs.claimCeiling: Cross-disciplinary design program requiring human-factors and accessibility research.

history.orientation: Constructive Humanist Agentics joins humanism and the capability tradition with cybernetics, human-computer symbiosis, participatory design, value-sensitive design, and responsible AI. It treats agency as something to enlarge while keeping authorization, standing, consequence, responsibility, and repair attached.

historicalArc.development: Human dignity, autonomy, education, participation, and public reason were developed as conditions of legitimate social order.
Feedback, control, automation, and interactive computing raised the question of how machines should extend rather than displace human judgment.
Design traditions increasingly required affected people, values, fairness, accountability, and social context to enter technical development.

buildsFrom.author: J. C. R. Licklider
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for interactive systems that augment human reasoning rather than simply automate it.

buildsFrom.author: Douglas Engelbart
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for tools designed to increase collective human problem-solving capacity.

buildsFrom.author: Joseph Weizenbaum
buildsFrom.relation: Critical lineage for limits, responsibility, and the difference between computational ability and legitimate judgment.

buildsFrom.author: Amartya Sen
buildsFrom.relation: Capability lineage for evaluating systems by the substantive agency people retain.

buildsFrom.author: Batya Friedman and Peter H. Kahn Jr.
buildsFrom.relation: Value-sensitive design lineage for integrating human values into technical systems.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The philosophy emerged from the recurring requirement that amplified agency must not dissolve human responsibility.
The Agency Audit translated that concern into operational tests of authorization, boundedness, legibility, contestability, attribution, and repair.
Public-agency doctrine extended the same structure to organizations, institutions, software, and essential systems.
aimsToward: A practical constitutional philosophy for delegated and artificial agency.
Agentic systems that preserve affected-party standing, human override, bounded authority, and viable repair.
A credible audit and assurance practice grounded in evidence rather than values language alone.

label: Mathematics & Formal Structures
short: Geometry, topology, analysis, logic, number theory, operators, and formal proof programs.
title: Mathematics tests whether the mechanics can be made exact.
body: Boundary First Labs develops formal and computational structures for studying distinction, representation, boundary, admissibility, invariant, closure, transport, defect, reconstruction, and repair. The mathematics lane contains exact definitions, comparative interpretations, finite computations, theorem targets, and proof programs. It is governed separately from physics so that mathematical coherence is never mistaken for empirical truth and physical plausibility is never mistaken for proof.
takeaways: Define the object and operating domain before generalizing.
Separate interpretation, construction, computation, conjecture, and theorem.
Promote finite results to continuum claims only through explicit proof.
Do not convert famous-problem proximity into solved-result language.
Make proof obligations and counterexample risks visible.
claims: Mathematics and physics may share objects while retaining different standards of validation.

validationStandard: A mathematical claim advances through exact definition, domain declaration, internal consistency, comparison with established structures, construction or computation, proof obligations, proof, and independent verification.

researchStatusLegend.seed: A mathematical direction or theorem shape exists, but core definitions, comparisons, or proof obligations remain incomplete.
researchStatusLegend.formalized: The principal objects, domain, terminology, claim boundary, and next proof questions are defined.
researchStatusLegend.computation-ready: A bounded symbolic, numerical, or finite experiment can be implemented with explicit success and failure criteria.
researchStatusLegend.theorem-target: A precise theorem or proposition has been stated with identified lemmas, counterexample risks, and proof obligations.
researchStatusLegend.proved: A proof has been completed, checked against its declared assumptions, and prepared for independent verification.

publicReadinessLegend.public: Safe to explain publicly with the present claim boundary.
publicReadinessLegend.publishable-with-revision: Substantively organized but still requires references, proof cleanup, computation, or expert review.
publicReadinessLegend.internal: Retain within the research program until definitions, comparisons, or dependencies are consolidated.
publicReadinessLegend.constrained: High-rigor or famous-problem-adjacent work requiring staged disclosure and explicit anti-overclaim controls.

researchPrograms.title: Envelope and Geometry Programs
researchPrograms.description: Studies how mathematical behavior changes when the envelope defining distance, volume, adjacency, or closure is changed, and which structures survive the change.
topics: L1, L2, Linfinity, and Lp norm-ball ladder
proofObligations: State the parameterized family and domain precisely.
Separate finite-dimensional identities from asymptotic or continuum claims.
Identify invariants under change of geometry gauge.
Compare new terminology with established convex and metric geometry.
safeClaims: The program organizes a family of exact and computational questions about changing geometric envelopes.
Several finite-dimensional kernels and comparisons are available for direct analysis.
prohibitedClaims: A universal geometry has been derived.
Finite norm-ball or volume identities establish broad physical or metaphysical conclusions.

researchPrograms.title: Boundary, Shell & Reconstruction Mathematics
researchPrograms.description: Asks what boundary package is sufficient to reconstruct a system and what information is lost or distorted by shell elimination, boundary response, or local-to-global assembly.
topics: Heat traces and spectral zeta functions
proofObligations: Prove finite elimination identities before continuum promotion.
Specify uniqueness and stability conditions.
Separate exact reconstruction from approximate admissibility.
Identify non-reconstructible interior degrees of freedom.
safeClaims: The program connects the theory to established boundary-response and inverse-problem mathematics.
Finite shell and operator targets can be stated and tested independently.
prohibitedClaims: A boundary always determines an arbitrary interior.
Finite Schur-complement calculations prove continuum reconstruction in general.

researchPrograms.title: Topology, Homology & Obstruction
researchPrograms.description: Formalizes object persistence, observation, defect, repair, and obstruction through cycles, cocycles, pairings, filtrations, compactifications, and local-to-global assembly.
proofObligations: Define the chain complexes and functorial maps.
Show when a defect class is exact, obstructive, or generative.
Separate pedagogical analogy from a new theorem.
Test invariance under refinement and representation change.
safeClaims: Homology and cohomology provide established structures for formalizing persistence and obstruction.
The lab is developing domain-specific pairings and defect classifications within that machinery.
prohibitedClaims: All objects or observers are literally homology or cohomology classes.
The proposed classification is universal before domain-specific proofs exist.

researchPrograms.title: Inscribed-Square & Geometric-Existence Research
researchPrograms.description: Develops symmetric constraints, configuration-space compactification, boundary-stratum analysis, parity or degree methods, and computational search for inscribed-square existence on Jordan curves.
proofObligations: Specify the compactified configuration space.
Control degenerate and coincident configurations.
Prove the relevant degree, parity, or intersection invariant.
Separate computational evidence from existence proof.
safeClaims: The program supplies a concrete symbolic and topological framework for studying the problem.
Computational search can test formulations and expose boundary failures.
prohibitedClaims: The inscribed-square problem has been solved.
A numerical search establishes the general theorem.

researchPrograms.title: Complex Analysis & Continuation
researchPrograms.description: Interprets continuation as transport of representation and classifies zero, finite, branch, essential, and generative defects using classical analytic and operator-theoretic structures.
proofObligations: Map each defect term to established analytic definitions.
State any generalized continuation operator precisely.
Prove coherence and uniqueness where claimed.
Distinguish reinterpretation from a new analytic result.
safeClaims: Continuation provides a rigorous mathematical setting for studying transport, gluing, singularity, and obstruction.
The lab is developing a defect-aware synthesis and extension program around these structures.
prohibitedClaims: Classical analytic continuation is replaced by a new theory.
Natural boundaries or essential singularities have been generally resolved.

researchPrograms.title: Logic, Foundations & Proof Envelopes
researchPrograms.description: Studies the representational and admissibility conditions required for formal systems, diagonal arguments, theorem support, contextual logic, and transfinite defect filtrations.
proofObligations: Preserve exact statements of established incompleteness and undecidability results.
Define any generalized diagonal-defect theorem independently.
Identify the minimum formal assumptions for each construction.
Avoid transporting conclusions across incompatible logical regimes.
safeClaims: The program compares established foundational limits through a common representational vocabulary.
Proof-envelope analysis can be developed as a companion to reverse-mathematical questions.
prohibitedClaims: Godel, Turing, or Cantor have been superseded.
A shared interpretation is itself a new impossibility theorem.

researchPrograms.title: Number Theory & Prime Structure
researchPrograms.description: Investigates prime generation, sieve survival, prefix-tree structure, multiplicative phase, spectral organization, and candidate fertility measures through reproducible computation and bounded conjectures.
proofObligations: Publish exact algorithms and datasets.
Compare against standard probabilistic and analytic number theory baselines.
Separate observed finite patterns from asymptotic claims.
State conjectures in conventional mathematical language.
safeClaims: Several finite prime and prefix-tree experiments can be reproduced.
Theoretical interpretations remain conjectural until connected to established number theory.
prohibitedClaims: The Riemann Hypothesis or twin-prime conjecture has been solved.
Finite computational patterns establish asymptotic prime laws.

researchPrograms.title: Tetration, Transcendence & Phase-Scale Transport
researchPrograms.description: Explores complex-height iteration, Abel and Kneser functional equations, tetradic holonomy, logarithmic covers, phase-to-scale transport, and higher-order analytic domains.
proofObligations: Define the tetration branch and normalization.
Compare with established tetration literature.
Specify holonomy observables and branch dependence.
Separate numerical continuation from analytic existence or uniqueness.
safeClaims: The program identifies a set of computational and analytic questions around complex iteration.
Several candidate observables can be tested numerically once definitions are fixed.
prohibitedClaims: A general tetration theory has been completed.
Numerical phase patterns establish transcendence results.

researchPrograms.title: Classical Geometry & Mathematical On-Ramps
researchPrograms.description: Uses established constructions and paradoxes to teach boundary, closure, defect, measure, resolution, constructibility, and admissibility without claiming replacement proofs.
topics: Squaring the circle and constructibility closure
proofObligations: Present the classical result accurately.
Label new diagrams and interpretations as pedagogical or comparative.
Avoid implying a novel proof when none is supplied.
Test whether the on-ramp improves understanding.
safeClaims: Classical results provide concrete public entrances into the research vocabulary.
Visual and computational artifacts can be built and evaluated as teaching tools.
prohibitedClaims: A new proof is present merely because the result has been reinterpreted.
A pedagogical analogy establishes the general theory.

researchPrograms.title: Deep-Problem Target Register
researchPrograms.description: Maintains explicitly bounded reformulations, operators, experiments, and proof obligations associated with famous open problems without converting them into solved-result claims.
proofObligations: State the standard problem exactly.
Identify the genuinely new object or reduction.
Prove equivalence before claiming progress on the original problem.
Seek domain-expert review before public promotion.
safeClaims: The register contains research targets and candidate reformulations.
Items enter the register only when the corpus contains a specific operator, experiment, or proof obligation.
prohibitedClaims: Any listed Millennium or famous open problem has been solved.
A suggestive reformulation counts as mathematical progress without equivalence or proof.

nextResearchActions: Create a canonical mathematics index linking every program to source artifacts and replacement history.
Select one finite theorem target, one computational experiment, and one public on-ramp for complete publication pipelines.
Separate finite, asymptotic, continuum, and universality claims in every formal artifact.
Obtain expert comparison for the inscribed-square, continuation, number-theory, and deep-problem lanes.
Publish negative results and failed proof paths where they clarify the boundary of the program.
coreThesis: Develops exact structures and proof programs for distinction, boundary, admissibility, closure, defect, reconstruction, and invariant preservation.

history.orientation: The mathematics lane builds from the long movement from classical geometry and analysis toward topology, operator theory, spectral geometry, algebraic structure, logic, and computation. Its recurring question is how boundary, invariant, closure, reconstruction, obstruction, and continuation can be made exact.

historicalArc.development: Geometry, measure, differential equations, complex analysis, and boundary-value problems established the mathematical study of form, limit, flux, and reconstruction.
Topology, set theory, functional analysis, spectral theory, and mathematical logic expanded what counted as structure and proof.
Category theory, sheaves, homology, operator algebras, numerical methods, and computer-assisted experimentation connected local data, global structure, and formal computation.

label: Physics & Physical Regimes
short: Fields, matter, spacetime, quantum regimes, gravity, thermodynamics, cosmology, and physical computation.
title: Physics tests whether the mechanics describe nature.
body: Boundary First Labs studies whether physical laws and regimes can be understood through boundary conditions, scale, spectral structure, invariant preservation, admissible transformation, closure, and defect. The physics lane is presented independently from mathematics because a coherent formal construction does not become physical until it is dimensionally valid, recovers established results, produces a distinct model or prediction, and survives comparison with observation. High-risk derivations and unification-adjacent programs remain explicitly constrained.
takeaways: Mathematical consistency is necessary but not sufficient for physical truth.
Audit dimensions, limits, known-physics recovery, numerical reproduction, literature, and data.
Separate interpretation, hypothesis, model, derivation, simulation, prediction, and result.
Publish failure and sensitivity, not only numerical agreement.
Use constrained disclosure for high-overclaim and unification-adjacent work.
Conjecture is a legitimate scholarly object when its assumptions, claim ceiling, and failure conditions are explicit.
A simulation establishes behavior of a model; it does not by itself establish behavior of nature.
Publish promising routes, failed routes, and unresolved obligations without promoting them into results.
claims: The mathematics lane demonstrates exactness; the physics lane demonstrates contact with nature.
Conjectural physics may be published responsibly when interpretation, formal status, physical status, evidence, and non-claims remain visibly separated.

sharedBridge.label: Mathematical Physics
sharedBridge.description: Shared work in spectral geometry, operator theory, boundary-value problems, PDEs, variational mechanics, Noether theory, heat kernels, quantum foundations, gauge structures, and geometric models of physical parameters.
sharedBridge.rule: A mathematically coherent structure receives a separate physics maturity label and may not inherit empirical status from its formal status.

validationStandard: A physical claim advances through dimensional audit, mathematical consistency, recovery of established physics, numerical reproduction, literature comparison, explicit observables, falsifiable prediction, empirical test, and external review.

researchStatusLegend.seed: A physical hypothesis or model direction exists, but equations, dimensions, comparisons, or observables remain incomplete.
researchStatusLegend.formalized: The objects, equations or operator targets, physical regime, assumptions, and claim boundary are defined.
researchStatusLegend.derivation-ready: A bounded derivation can be audited for units, consistency, limiting behavior, and recovery of established physics.
researchStatusLegend.simulation-ready: A numerical model, baseline, data source, metrics, and falsification criteria can be implemented.
researchStatusLegend.model-tested: At least one derivation or simulation has been reproduced and compared with established theory or data.
researchStatusLegend.empirically-supported: A distinct prediction or explanatory gain has survived meaningful empirical comparison and independent review.

publicReadinessLegend.public: Safe to explain publicly as an interpretation, bounded model, or reviewed research question.
publicReadinessLegend.publishable-with-revision: Ready for technical cleanup, references, derivation detail, simulation, or expert review.
publicReadinessLegend.internal: Retain within the research program until equations, dimensions, observables, and comparisons are consolidated.
publicReadinessLegend.constrained: High-overclaim, high-leverage, or unification-adjacent work requiring staged disclosure and formal audit.

researchPrograms.title: Volumology & Boundary-First Physics
researchPrograms.description: Studies physical systems as bounded, layered, spectral, scale-dependent regions and asks how volume, boundary, bulk, flux, persistence, and reconstruction relate across physical regimes.
validationGates: Separate established mathematical physics from new ontology.
Write explicit models for at least one classical regime.
Recover standard observables in the zero-defect limit.
Identify a distinct calculational or predictive advantage.
safeClaims: Volumology is a proposed mathematical-physics branch within the lab.
It organizes questions about bounded regions, interfaces, bulk structure, spectra, and reconstruction.
prohibitedClaims: Volumology is an established physical theory.
The framework replaces existing physics without explicit equations and tests.

researchPrograms.title: Variational Mechanics, Action & Noether Theory
researchPrograms.description: Begins with standard variational calculus, retains explicit boundary or shell defect terms, recovers ordinary conservation in the zero-defect case, and derives modified balance laws when those terms remain.
validationGates: Complete unit and sign audits.
Derive Euler-Lagrange and Noether identities explicitly.
Recover standard conservation laws when defects vanish.
Compare retained terms with open-system, flux, and anomaly literature.
safeClaims: The program targets explicit defect-aware variational identities.
Standard Noether theory must be recovered as the limiting case.
prohibitedClaims: A new law of nature has been derived before equations and limits are checked.
Boundary terms alone imply new physical phenomena.

researchPrograms.title: Classical Fields & Boundary-Determined Dynamics
researchPrograms.description: Applies boundary response, flux, Green functions, gauge conditions, and spectral reconstruction to electromagnetism, wave equations, scattering, and related classical fields.
validationGates: Use standard field equations and units.
Specify boundary data and well-posedness.
Recover conventional solutions.
Demonstrate a new diagnostic, numerical, or interpretive result.
safeClaims: Classical field theory offers a rigorous test domain for boundary and reconstruction methods.
The program seeks concrete models rather than restating that boundary conditions matter.
prohibitedClaims: Maxwell theory has been replaced.
A boundary interpretation is a distinct physical prediction by itself.

researchPrograms.title: Relativity, Gravitation & Spacetime Volume
researchPrograms.description: Investigates spacetime regions, curvature, gravitational action, horizons, shell decompositions, causal closure, observer-relative representation, and information transport across relativistic boundaries.
validationGates: Audit all source material for speculative generation.
Write coordinate-invariant equations.
Recover Einsteinian solutions and limits.
Compare with ADM, boundary-action, horizon, and quasi-local literature.
Identify an observable or calculational difference.
safeClaims: The lane contains research questions and mathematical-physics comparisons.
No alternative gravitational theory is presently established.
prohibitedClaims: General relativity has been replaced or unified with quantum mechanics.
A geometric analogy constitutes a gravitational field equation.

researchPrograms.title: Quantum Foundations & State-Space Closure
researchPrograms.description: Studies Hilbert-space representation, unitary evolution, measurement, decoherence, tensor composition, observability, quantum error, and repair through explicit operator structures and admissible projection.
validationGates: Define the Hilbert spaces and operator algebra.
Preserve unitarity, positivity, and normalization where required.
Recover Born-rule and standard measurement predictions.
Separate interpretation from altered dynamics.
Identify an empirical discriminator before claiming new physics.
safeClaims: The program compares quantum structures with the lab vocabulary through explicit operators.
Any modified dynamics must first recover standard quantum mechanics in its declared domain.
prohibitedClaims: The measurement problem or quantum gravity has been solved.
Interpretive correspondence establishes a new quantum theory.

researchPrograms.title: Planck Regime & Quantum-Gravity Coupling
researchPrograms.description: Investigates whether the Planck regime can be modeled as a coupling boundary between quantum state representation and relativistic spacetime representation, including scale saturation and ultraviolet closure conditions.
validationGates: Define a mathematical state space and coupling operator.
Preserve dimensional consistency.
Recover quantum and relativistic limits.
Compare with quantum-gravity and emergent-spacetime literature.
Derive a falsifiable consequence or no-go result.
safeClaims: This is a conjectural research program about coupled representation at the Planck regime.
The present work does not constitute a unification theory.
prohibitedClaims: Quantum mechanics and general relativity have been unified.
The Planck scale has been derived from the present framework.

researchPrograms.title: Particle, Gauge, Clifford & Standard Model Research
researchPrograms.description: Compares gauge structures, Lie and Clifford algebras, spectral triples, noncommutative geometry, spin, charge, and particle representations with the boundary and admissibility framework.
validationGates: Map every proposed object to standard algebraic definitions.
Recover the Standard Model representation content before extension.
Avoid parameter fitting disguised as derivation.
Identify a calculational or empirical distinction.
safeClaims: The program is comparative and exploratory.
Established gauge and spectral structures provide a disciplined literature base for evaluation.
prohibitedClaims: The Standard Model has been derived or replaced.
Algebraic resemblance proves a physical identification.

researchPrograms.title: Fine-Structure Constant Geometric Derivation Audit
researchPrograms.description: Investigates whether the fine-structure constant admits a genuinely non-fitted geometric or spectral derivation through six-dimensional decompositions, boundary products, heat-kernel or zeta structures, Dirichlet-to-Neumann response, or spectral stiffness.
validationGates: Complete unit and dimensional audit.
Eliminate hidden fitting and back-solving.
Reproduce every numerical step from source.
Compare with known derivation and numerology literature.
Quantify sensitivity and uncertainty.
Obtain independent expert review.
safeClaims: A restricted audit is examining candidate geometric and spectral derivations.
The current material is not a validated first-principles derivation.
prohibitedClaims: Boundary First Labs has derived alpha from first principles.
Numerical proximity without independent assumptions constitutes a derivation.

researchPrograms.title: PDEs, Flow & Weather
researchPrograms.claimClass: PDE interpretation and empirical simulation program
researchPrograms.description: Develops defect profiles, boundary and flux diagnostics, regime classification, multiscale weather simulation, forecast-error correction, and public testbeds while preserving standard PDE and numerical-weather baselines.
validationGates: Use standard PDE benchmarks and conservation checks.
Define numerical grids, stability, and convergence tests.
Compare against operational or accepted baselines.
Separate reinterpretation from regularity proof.
Publish forecast and simulation failures.
safeClaims: Weather and flow provide bounded empirical testbeds for multiscale boundary transport.
The Navier-Stokes work is presently interpretive and experimental, not a regularity proof.
prohibitedClaims: The Navier-Stokes Millennium problem has been solved.
A new weather framework replaces operational numerical weather prediction before benchmark evidence.

researchPrograms.title: Thermodynamics, Heat & Spectral Emergence
researchPrograms.description: Studies heat flow, entropy, coarse-graining, irreversible loss, spectral density, state counting, horizon entropy, and nonequilibrium defect accumulation through admissible forgetting and boundary transport.
validationGates: Recover standard thermodynamic identities.
Distinguish information-theoretic, statistical, and physical entropy.
Specify ensembles and coarse-graining maps.
Derive measurable consequences rather than analogy alone.
safeClaims: The lane develops comparisons between admissible forgetting, spectral structure, and established thermodynamic formalisms.
No new thermodynamic law is presently claimed.
prohibitedClaims: Entropy has been reduced to a single representational definition.
Heat-kernel analogies establish physical emergence without a model.

researchPrograms.title: Cosmology & Global Closure
researchPrograms.description: Maintains emerging questions about observable domains, CMB boundary records, cosmological horizons, ultraviolet-to-infrared scale ladders, dark-sector representation, and global causal closure.
validationGates: Source every claim in current cosmology literature.
Write a background spacetime and perturbation model.
Recover standard cosmological observables.
Identify a distinct prediction and dataset.
Obtain expert review before public promotion.
safeClaims: This is an emerging research register, not a mature cosmological model.
The questions are retained for structured development and comparison.
prohibitedClaims: The dark sector, early universe, or cosmological horizons have been explained.
A global closure metaphor is a cosmological solution.

nextResearchActions: Create a canonical physics index linking each hypothesis, derivation, and model to source artifacts and claim ceilings.
Complete dimensional and numerical audits before public promotion of fine-structure, Planck-regime, gravity, and cosmology materials.
Select one variational derivation and one weather or flow simulation for complete reproducible pipelines.
Establish known-physics recovery tests for every proposed model.
Build an external review network spanning mathematical physics, quantum theory, relativity, field theory, fluid dynamics, and cosmology.
Launch the Physics Outlooks, Conjectures & Research Notes series with a visible claim-status template.
Select one interpretive outlook, one derivation attempt, and one simulation-oriented note for the first publication set.
Create public derivation, simulation, and negative-result ledgers for the physics program.
coreThesis: Tests whether boundary, scale, spectral, invariant, closure, and defect structures yield valid and empirically accountable physical models.

history.orientation: The physics lane builds from classical mechanics, fields, thermodynamics, relativity, quantum theory, and mathematical physics. Its boundary-first emphasis follows an established truth of physics—boundary conditions, symmetries, observables, and scales matter—while asking whether a more unified representational account can produce precise models or predictions.

historicalArc.development: Action principles, differential equations, conservation laws, and field boundaries organized physical dynamics.
Spacetime, state spaces, observables, measurement, uncertainty, and scale transformed the physical meaning of representation.
Gauge theory, operator methods, spectral geometry, information, horizons, renormalization, and numerical simulation connected local laws to global structure and scale.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The historical Volumology program explored physical regions, boundaries, shells, spectra, and reconstruction.

The lane was reorganized into explicit programs for variational mechanics, fields, relativity, quantum foundations, Planck-regime coupling, particles and gauge structure, flow and weather, thermodynamics, and cosmology.
High-risk claims—especially the fine-structure, Planck-regime, and unification material—were placed behind dimensional, mathematical, numerical, literature, empirical, and external-review gates.
aimsToward: Mathematically explicit models that recover known physics before claiming novelty.
Bounded simulations and observations capable of distinguishing a Boundary First model from established alternatives.
A disciplined account of where representation, scale, boundary, and admissibility become physically measurable rather than merely interpretive.
history.citationNote: Representative lineage, not a claim of derivation or equivalence. Before publication, verify editions, translations, page references, and the exact relation of each citation to the local claim.

series.title: Boundary-First Physics: Outlooks, Conjectures & Research Notes
series.purpose: Publish physically interesting implications, bounded conjectures, toy models, attempted derivations, simulations, negative results, and research outlooks before they are mature enough to be presented as established physical results.
series.publicPosture: The series makes uncertain work inspectable, citable, criticizable, and developable without concealing its uncertainty or inflating its authority.
series.governingPrinciple: Do not wait for every conjecture to become a result. Make each conjecture mature enough to become a legitimate object of criticism.
notAClaimOf: physical truth inferred from numerical resemblance alone

artifactClasses.label: Physical Interpretation
artifactClasses.definition: Re-describes an established physical object, theory, or process through Boundary First terminology without claiming a new prediction or replacement theory.
minimumBurden: Identify the established physical formulation.
Map terms precisely rather than by loose analogy.
State what the reinterpretation adds and what it leaves unchanged.

artifactClasses.label: Physics Outlook
artifactClasses.definition: Describes a bounded research direction and the formal or empirical work that would be required to make it physically consequential.
minimumBurden: Name the target problem and neighboring literature.
State the proposed bridge or organizing question.
List recovery obligations, risks, and next tests.

artifactClasses.label: Conjecture
artifactClasses.definition: States a specific proposition precisely enough to admit mathematical analysis, computation, comparison, or physical refutation.
minimumBurden: Define every operative term.
Declare assumptions and regime.
State at least one failure or falsification condition.

artifactClasses.label: Toy Model
artifactClasses.definition: Constructs a simplified mathematical system to determine whether a proposed mechanism is coherent and nontrivial.
minimumBurden: Specify the model and simplifications.
Separate model behavior from claims about nature.
Show what stronger model would be needed next.

artifactClasses.label: Derivation Attempt
artifactClasses.definition: Presents a transparent route toward a known or proposed physical quantity while exposing every assumption, normalization, unit, and unresolved step.
minimumBurden: Complete a dimensional and dependency ledger.
Disclose inserted constants, fitted values, and normalization choices.
Publish sensitivity, alternative routes, and failed steps.

artifactClasses.label: Simulation or Computational Result
artifactClasses.definition: Reports reproducible numerical behavior of a defined model, baseline, or diagnostic.
minimumBurden: Publish model, parameters, code or executable procedure, and metrics.
Compare against accepted baselines.
State that model evidence is not automatically evidence about nature.

artifactClasses.label: Physical Hypothesis
artifactClasses.definition: Advances a distinct claim about observable reality that could, in principle, be tested against physical evidence.
minimumBurden: Pass dimensional and mathematical consistency checks.
Recover relevant established physics.
Identify a distinct observable, prediction, or discriminating test.

artifactClasses.label: Supported Physical Result
artifactClasses.definition: Reports a physical claim that has survived meaningful empirical comparison, independent scrutiny, and replication appropriate to its scope.
minimumBurden: Document data, uncertainty, alternatives, and independent review.
State the exact evidential scope.
Preserve correction and replication paths.

defaultLanguage.intendedUse: Criticism, comparison, formalization, and research development
defaultLanguage.nonClaims: No proof, completed derivation, empirical confirmation, or replacement of established physics is claimed unless separately demonstrated.

standardPublicationStructure.purpose: State the conventional theory, objects, results, and literature on which the note depends.
Identify what the established formulation distinguishes, preserves, idealizes, compresses, or leaves unresolved.
Explain how boundary, scale, invariant, admissibility, closure, or defect reorganizes the question.
State the new possibility at the narrowest defensible claim level.
Define the equation, operator, state space, boundary package, action, transformation, or toy model needed to make the proposal precise.
List the established results, limits, dimensions, symmetries, or observables the proposal must reproduce.
State what the proposal might explain, calculate, predict, organize, or make easier to test.
State what would make the proposal wrong, trivial, redundant, numerological, or physically irrelevant.
Specify the next derivation, simulation, comparison, dataset, or external review.
Separate established result, interpretation, inference, conjecture, speculation, and unresolved question.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Physics as a Hierarchy of Closure Regimes
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Compares how classical mechanics, fields, relativity, quantum theory, thermodynamics, and quantum field theory close around different state, boundary, symmetry, observable, and scale structures.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A comparative vocabulary and research outlook, not a reduction of all physics to one theory.
nextObligations: Map each physical regime to its canonical formalism.
Demonstrate that closure language adds discriminatory value.
Identify cases where the comparison fails.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Volumology and Boundary-First Physical Ontology
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Places the historical Volumology work as the mathematical-physics study of region, boundary, shell, flux, volume, scale, spectral response, persistence, and boundary-to-bulk reconstruction.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A proposed research branch and ontology, not an established replacement for physical theory.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Defect-Modified Noether Mechanics
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Retains explicit boundary or unresolved-defect terms in variational mechanics, recovers standard Noether conservation when they vanish, and studies the resulting balance laws when they remain.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A derivation program until the identities are explicit and compared with established boundary, source, flux, anomaly, and open-system results.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Quantum Measurement as Admissible Projection
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Studies measurement as a projection from a richer state representation into an observationally closed outcome regime and asks what is preserved, lost, contextualized, or rendered inaccessible.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: An interpretation and formal research question, not a settled interpretation of quantum mechanics.
nextObligations: Define the projection and admissibility condition.
Compare with decoherence, coarse-graining, conditionalization, and measurement theory.
Identify whether the framing yields a new formal result.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Planck-Regime Coupled Closure
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Investigates whether quantum state-space representation and relativistic spacetime representation cease to remain independently admissible in an extreme-scale regime.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A conjectural coupling question, not a unification result.
nextObligations: Define both closure structures and their invariants.
Specify the coupling and failure of separate admissibility.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Boundary-Spectral Physical Regime Atlas
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Organizes eigenmodes, resonances, propagators, heat kernels, scattering data, spectral density, and boundary response into a disciplined comparative atlas of physical regimes.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A research and comparison framework until it yields a distinct theorem, calculation, or empirical discriminator.
nextObligations: Show where the atlas improves classification or calculation.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Research Ledger Toward a Possible Geometric or Spectral Derivation of the Fine-Structure Constant
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Publishes the derivation route as a transparent ledger of assumptions, normalizations, units, numerical sensitivity, alternatives, failures, and literature comparison.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A documented derivation program; no first-principles derivation is claimed unless every dependency and audit gate is passed.
nextObligations: Compare against known derivation and numerology literature.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Thermodynamics and Admissible Forgetting
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Compares admissible forgetting with coarse-graining, entropy, irreversible loss, macroscopic closure, and scale-dependent representation in established statistical mechanics.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A comparative and formalization program, not a new thermodynamic law.
nextObligations: Separate physical, statistical, and information-theoretic entropy.

candidatePublicationProgram.title: Weather as a Testbed for Multiscale Boundary Transport
candidatePublicationProgram.summary: Uses weather and flow as severe empirical benchmarks for multiscale transport, boundary error, regime detection, ensemble ranking, forecast divergence, and defect-guided correction.
candidatePublicationProgram.claimCeiling: A proposed benchmark and modeling program, not a replacement for operational numerical weather prediction.
nextObligations: Choose public datasets and operational baselines.

recommended: The following conjecture is speculative and precise enough to be worth pursuing.
We do not claim that this mechanism occurs in nature; we claim that it defines a coherent physical question that can be formalized and tested.
This note presents a possible bridge, not a completed crossing.
The proposal should be judged by whether it recovers established results, produces a nontrivial calculation, and exposes a path to empirical failure.
The numerical agreement reported here concerns the stated model and does not by itself establish a physical derivation.

releaseRules: Every artifact carries the mandatory claim-status box.
Every conjecture states assumptions, operating regime, and at least one failure condition.
Every derivation attempt publishes units, dependencies, normalizations, and sensitivity.
Every simulation distinguishes evidence about the model from evidence about nature.
Every physical hypothesis states known-physics recovery obligations and a discriminating observable or test.
Negative results, abandoned routes, and corrected formulations remain part of the public research record.
Constrained topics may publish conceptual outlooks while withholding operational or high-risk implementation detail.
No artifact inherits empirical authority from the mathematical maturity of a neighboring result.

label: Computational & Machine Intelligence
short: Learning, graphs, knowledge, complexity, memory, and computational closure.
title: Computation is a representational regime.
body: This research program studies computation, machine learning, memory, knowledge systems, graphs, complexity, compression, and artificial agency through Representational Mechanics. It asks not only whether an algorithm runs or a model predicts, but what distinctions it preserves, which boundaries authorize transport, what may be forgotten, where defects accumulate, how local relations compose, and when a computational result is admissible for deployment. The portfolio includes public concept papers, experiment-ready architectures, internal foundational programs, and tightly constrained conjectural work.
takeaways: Choose computational representations by the invariants they must preserve.
Treat edges, models, memories, schemas, and interfaces as consequential transport claims.
Separate interpretations, architectures, experiments, conjectures, and demonstrated results.
Measure defect, calibration, composition, provenance, and repair—not task performance alone.
Do not promote high-rigor research programs into result claims before formalization and independent review.
claims: A high-similarity computational relation may still be defective when it crosses an unsupported boundary.
Learning can be studied as admissible representation refinement under context.
Computational knowledge should remain sourced, defensible, revisable, transportable, and repairable.
Local computational validity does not guarantee global compositional admissibility.
Complexity and quantum-computation interpretations in this portfolio remain research programs rather than solved results.

coreThesis: Computational and learning systems should be studied by the distinctions they form, the boundaries and invariants they preserve, the defects they generate, and the conditions under which their transformations remain admissible.
productRelationship: Computational research is not merely implementation support for the software portfolio. It produces independent theories, models, architectures, experiments, and constraints. Selected results may become software products or testbeds, while product use returns evidence and failure cases to the research program.
researchPortfolioThesis: Boundary First Labs studies what computation, learning, memory, knowledge, complexity, and artificial agency are doing mechanically—not only whether a system produces an output.
researchPrinciples: Every program must declare its claim class and maturity.
Every experiment-ready program should name baselines, metrics, ablations, and failure criteria.
Safe public claims and prohibited result claims must be recorded separately.
Negative results refine the program and should be preserved.
Conjectural complexity and quantum work requires strict publication controls and external comparison to established literature.
High-leverage self-modifying and agentic architectures remain constrained until their authority, reversibility, and repair conditions are formalized.

A low-similarity path may be admissible and a high-similarity path may be defective.
prohibitedClaims: Edge admissibility solves hallucination, GNN robustness, or graph reasoning in general.
All graph edges are defective or all relations are transport maps.

researchPrograms.title: Phase-Defect Graphs
researchPrograms.description: An extension of edge admissibility in which edges carry phase or twist as well as magnitude, allowing loop holonomy and global nonclosure to be measured rather than inferred only from pairwise weights.
experiments: Synthetic graph benchmark with controllable phase loops.
Ordinary GCN, weighted GCN, phase-edge GNN, and holonomy-loss comparison.
Deletion, insertion, and cycle-inconsistency corruption tests.
safeClaims: Phase-defect graphs provide a way to represent and test global nonclosure using edge phase and loop holonomy.
prohibitedClaims: Phase-defect graphs are already a new field.
Phase-defect graphs generally outperform standard GNNs or solve graph reasoning.

researchPrograms.title: Computational Epistemology
researchPrograms.description: The study of how computation produces, represents, tests, transports, repairs, and closes knowledge while preserving provenance, claim status, criticism, and replacement history.
experiments: Auditable corpus-ingestion pipeline.
Claim, evidence, provenance, defect, and invariant ledger generation.
Summary-only versus provenance-preserving workflow comparison.
safeClaims: Computational epistemology is a useful organizing frame for corpus refinement, knowledge compilation, provenance tracking, claim discipline, and AI-assisted research workflows.
prohibitedClaims: Computational epistemology is already a finished formal theory of knowledge.
It replaces philosophy, databases, knowledge representation, or the scientific method.

researchPrograms.title: MapReduce as Epistemic Algebra
researchPrograms.description: A reading of map as local witness extraction, filter as admissibility testing, groupBy as boundary or equivalence formation, and reduce as closure over grouped evidence.
experiments: Implement the corpus-forging pipeline as explicit map, filter, groupBy, reduce, and critic stages.
Compare auditability and defect visibility against narrative summarization.
safeClaims: MapReduce provides a useful computational metaphor and implementation pattern for auditable corpus refinement.
prohibitedClaims: MapReduce by itself is a general theory of knowledge.

researchPrograms.title: Distinction Computation & Closure Machines
researchPrograms.description: An emerging program studying effective computation through distinction, persistence, inspection, admissible transformation, grammar, and closure, including possible Distinction–Turing and Closure–Turing equivalence questions.
researchPrograms.sourceStatus: Developed in prior project discussions; requires consolidated formal artifact and comparison to established models of computation.
experiments: Define a minimal distinction-and-closure machine.
Translate finite automata, grammars, Turing machines, reversible systems, and probabilistic systems into the proposed vocabulary.
Search for equivalence proofs or counterexamples.
safeClaims: This is an emerging foundational research program about the minimal representational machinery of effective computation.
prohibitedClaims: Closure–Turing equivalence or a Distinction–Turing thesis has been proved.
The proposed machinery replaces established computation theory.

researchPrograms.title: Complexity, Certificates & Reconstruction
researchPrograms.description: A high-rigor program interpreting verification and construction through certificate observability, polynomially stable reconstruction, computational gauges, and possible obstruction or twist invariants.
experiments: Define certificate boundary and stable reconstruction precisely.
Test the proposed vocabulary on known P, NP, P-complete, and NP-complete examples.
Define or refute a reduction-monotone computational obstruction invariant.
safeClaims: The certificate-boundary and reconstruction language is a conjectural research framing.
The computational twist invariant is a theorem target, not an established invariant.
prohibitedClaims: Boundary First Labs has solved P versus NP.
The stated interpretive equivalences are established theorems.

researchPrograms.title: Quantum-Computational Admissibility
researchPrograms.description: An exploratory program examining classical projection, Hilbert-space reconstruction, simulation regimes, representation growth, and quantum advantage through admissibility and generative defect.
researchPrograms.sourceStatus: Present in the refined computational corpus as high-rigor research-program material; requires comparison to stabilizer, tensor-network, contextuality, and simulation literature.
experiments: Classify known classically simulable quantum regimes by bounded representation defect.
Compare representation growth and reconstruction cost across toy quantum systems.
Test whether the proposed framing adds explanatory or predictive value.
safeClaims: Quantum advantage can be investigated as a possible failure of admissible classical compression or reconstruction.
This is a research framing requiring comparison to established quantum-computation theory.
prohibitedClaims: The program has explained quantum advantage in general.
The program establishes a new quantum-complexity result.

researchPrograms.title: Boundary-Spectral Memory
researchPrograms.description: An emerging architecture for organizing persistent machine memory by boundary, scale, context, defect, provenance, and admissibility rather than recency or vector similarity alone.
researchPrograms.sourceStatus: Developed in prior project discussions; requires promotion into a formal architecture and experiment note.
experiments: Boundary-aware retrieval versus vector-only retrieval.
Defect-guided pruning and memory repair.
Scale-sensitive context assembly for long-running agents.
Persistent-assistant and Corpus Forge memory pilots.
safeClaims: Boundary-Spectral Memory is an emerging architecture direction for boundary-aware retrieval and persistent context.
prohibitedClaims: It has demonstrated superior long-context performance.
It solves persistent memory or agent orchestration.

researchPrograms.title: Lawful Self-Modifying Computation
researchPrograms.description: A research direction for programs and stored procedures that may revise their own operative grammar while preserving typed authority, protected invariants, inspectability, reversibility, and repair.
researchPrograms.sourceStatus: Developed in recent project discussions; formal model, literature comparison, and disclosure boundaries remain to be established.
experiments: Define a typed self-modification calculus.
Require proof obligations or executable checks for invariant preservation.
Test rollback, audit, and repair under bounded grammar modification.
safeClaims: Lawful self-modification is a constrained research direction centered on authority, invariants, reversibility, and repair.
prohibitedClaims: A safe general self-modifying agent architecture has been completed.
Self-modification is admissible without explicit governance and proof obligations.

researchPrograms.title: Admissible Compression & Isotropic Computing
researchPrograms.description: A draft program studying what computational representations may forget, how local relations compose across orientation and scale, when compression becomes defective, and whether alternative architectures can preserve more symmetric or boundary-aware structure.
experiments: Decompose the current draft into edge admissibility, phase-defect graphs, admissible compression, and architecture-specific claims.
Define compression invariants and counterexamples.
Compare boundary-aware compression with ordinary lossy representations on bounded tasks.
safeClaims: The existing draft contains several separable computational research lanes and should be decomposed before stronger public claims are made.
prohibitedClaims: Isotropic Computing is already a demonstrated superior computing architecture.
All compression can be characterized by the current theory.

researchPrograms.title: Ontological Representation Durability
researchPrograms.claimClass: synthetic benchmark protocol and representation study
researchPrograms.description: Tests semantic durability separately from linguistic fluency under paraphrase, renaming, composition, intervention, contradiction, ontology shift, trace, and repair controls.
safeClaims: The synthetic carrier validates metrics and failure modes.
It does not establish ontology-backed superiority.
prohibitedClaims: Ontological representations are generally superior.
Oracle structured input supports an end-to-end language claim.

researchPrograms.title: Separated Fluency and Ontology-Governed Transformation
researchPrograms.description: Separates language acquisition, ontology-governed transformation, and realization while matching parser and renderer controls.
safeClaims: Separation improves traceability and fault localization in the finite carrier.
Matched direct and separated systems are behaviorally near-equivalent.
prohibitedClaims: Architectural separation improves accuracy by itself.
A valid typed trace establishes semantic correctness.

researchPrograms.title: Multi-Domain Ontological Representation Benchmark
researchPrograms.claimClass: synthetic learned-model benchmark and external preregistration
researchPrograms.description: A 544-example four-domain corpus, matched lightweight learners, frozen extensions, provider-neutral adapter, and external execution gate.
safeClaims: The learned systems are near-equivalent in the current synthetic study.
The parser is the dominant observed bottleneck and wrong ontologies can remain trace-valid.
prohibitedClaims: The benchmark establishes pretrained-model or production performance.
Human fluency, domain validity, lower cost, or architecture superiority has been demonstrated.

nextResearchActions: Resolve exact external model access, spend authority, licensing, and named reviewer assignments before running the preregistered external pilot.

Treat no difference, baseline absorption, diagnostic-only value, or a negative result as valid outcomes.

mathematicsRelationship: Mathematics supplies exact graph, operator, spectral, topological, logical, and complexity structures used by the computational research program.
physicsRelationship: Physics supplies empirical and simulation domains for multiscale computation, field reconstruction, quantum computation, flow, weather, and model admissibility.
practiceBoundary: This node houses computational and machine-intelligence research: learning, graphs, knowledge, complexity, memory, compression, and foundations of computation. Established software-development methods, architecture patterns, delivery practice, and consulting belong in Software Engineering & Applied Computer Science, even when they draw upon the same representational vocabulary.

history.orientation: The computational lane builds from automata and computability, information theory, complexity, graph theory, knowledge representation, machine learning, and human-computer systems. It investigates computation as a representational regime without claiming that every reinterpretation is a new foundation.

historicalArc.development: Formal logic, recursive functions, automata, and universal machines established mathematical accounts of effective procedure.
Information theory, stored-program computers, algorithms, complexity classes, and graph methods organized computation at scale.
Statistical learning, neural networks, graph learning, knowledge graphs, retrieval, and agent systems shifted emphasis toward learned representation and adaptive behavior.

label: Boundary-First Engineering
short: Turn domain boundaries and invariants into executable systems.
title: Engineering begins before implementation.
body: Boundary-First Engineering is the applied professional practice that carries Boundary First and Representational Mechanics into the software-engineering and systems-practice portfolio. It discovers the domain before choosing the architecture: extracting actors, artifacts, cycles, pressures, boundaries, invariants, interfaces, contracts, admissible transformations, failure modes, consequences, and responsibility; building the smallest end-to-end skeleton; and letting real use expose defects before complexity hardens into code. The broader software practice then relates this method to Agile, Kanban, requirements engineering, Domain-Driven Design, architecture, patterns, technical leadership, maintenance, and consulting.
takeaways: Own the problem complexity.
Use the simplest representation that preserves the invariant.
Design each interface by deciding what it is allowed to forget.
Build the smallest thing that lets the real process close.
Make failure observable and repairable.
claims: Architecture should follow the domain's operative boundaries and protected invariants rather than precede their discovery.
Real end-to-end use exposes representational defects earlier than isolated component elaboration.
coreThesis: Boundary-First Engineering turns the Boundary First method, domain distinctions, invariants, admissibility conditions, and failure paths into executable and repairable systems.

history.orientation: Boundary-First Engineering applies the Boundary First method and builds from systems engineering, requirements engineering, domain modeling, software architecture, Lean and Agile discovery, safety engineering, and design science. Its synthesis is to discover the consequential domain before selecting the representation or architecture.

historicalArc.development: Engineering disciplines formalized requirements, interfaces, verification, lifecycle, and systems integration.
Modularity, information hiding, domain language, interfaces, and architectural boundaries became central to maintainable software.
Lean, Agile, evolutionary design, and product discovery treated delivery as a process of learning under uncertainty.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The method developed from repeated software and institutional work in which implementation choices arrived before the operative domain had become legible.
It was formalized around actors, artifacts, boundaries, invariants, interfaces, contracts, failure modes, responsibility, and the smallest end-to-end delivery skeleton.
Later revisions added pressure, cycles, admissibility contracts, licensed forgetting, affected-agent maps, and repair ownership.
aimsToward: A cross-domain method that can be used independently of the full theoretical corpus.
Worked cases demonstrating when boundary-first discovery changes architecture, delivery sequence, governance, or repair responsibility.
A professional practice with inspectable artifacts, explicit limits, and evidence proportionate to consequential use.
