label: Software Engineering & Applied Computer Science
short: Agile, Kanban, architecture, patterns, delivery, technical leadership, and consulting.
title: Software is discovered into a form that can close.
body: This lane develops a practitioner, design-science, and consulting body around software engineering and applied computer science. It does not claim to replace Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Lean, Domain-Driven Design, requirements engineering, Onion or Clean Architecture, ports and adapters, modular monoliths, microservices, software patterns, or established architecture and delivery practice. It recontextualizes them through boundary, invariant, closure, uncertainty, defect, consequence, and repair: asking what function each practice is meant to preserve, how it fails when reduced to ritual or fashion, and how teams can use it to stabilize the smallest coherent product form that satisfies real operational need under constraint. The research becomes field guides, method cards, architecture doctrine, case studies, workshops, technical leadership, project rescue, and software consulting.
takeaways: Extend established practice; do not erase its lineage.
Agile is a disciplined way to learn what reality will let close.
Kanban works when it makes flow, blockage, and work-in-progress visible.
Patterns are tools; invariants are the reason.
Architecture earns its keep when it preserves domain invariants under change.
Technical debt is accumulated closure failure.
Consulting should make hidden boundaries and failure modes explicit enough that useful delivery can resume.
claims: Software delivery can be studied as the stabilization of useful form under uncertainty.

Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Lean Startup, Domain-Driven Design, and architecture patterns can be interpreted as partial operational forms of closure-driven discovery without treating them as identical or claiming to replace them.
Many software patterns can be interpreted as reusable boundary moves that preserve invariants across interaction, lifecycle, failure, or representation change.
Architecture is the organization of nested regimes of knowledge, ownership, exposure, refusal, dependency, and failure.
Consequence-bearing software practice requires stronger records, observability, incident response, and named responsibility than ordinary low-consequence software work.
A consulting practice is credible when its methods change decisions, produce inspectable artifacts, and remain open to criticism and repair.
coreThesis: Software engineering becomes more reliable when established delivery, architecture, and pattern practices are evaluated by the boundaries, invariants, feedback, and repair paths they preserve.

included: Agile, Scrum, Kanban, Lean, and flow systems
Technical debt, refactoring, observability, reliability, and maintenance
Technical leadership, project rescue, consulting, training, and professional responsibility
excluded: Foundational claims about computation, complexity, quantum computation, or machine learning, which belong in Computational & Machine Intelligence
Individual software products and platforms, which belong in Software, Products & Testbeds
The general cross-domain method itself, which remains Boundary-First Engineering

relationshipToEstablishedPractice.boundaryFirstReading: An observational and adaptive system for discovering what product form can close under changing constraints.
A cadence and accountability structure whose ceremonies are useful only when they improve observation, coordination, and delivery rather than status theater.
A representation of flow, blockage, queueing, and work-in-progress that helps teams see where closure is prevented.
A system of working probes through which market, user, and operational reality can invalidate or stabilize a product hypothesis.
A discipline for protecting domain language, ownership, and invariant boundaries from accidental implementation coupling.
The extraction and testing of the conditions under which a real operational process can complete, not merely transcription of initial requests.
Families of boundary arrangements intended to protect core domain behavior from volatile interfaces and infrastructure.
Deployment and ownership choices whose validity depends on whether the selected boundaries match the domain’s actual closure structure.
Reusable boundary moves for preserving invariants under variation, interaction, failure, lifecycle change, or representation transport.
Mechanisms for detecting when the deployed system has crossed a defect boundary and for restoring a lawful path to repair.

instrumentStack: Rollback, Shutdown, Recovery, and Repair Protocol
Scoped Software Engineer of Record or Responsible Engineer role
practicePrograms.scopeBoundary: The stack is intended for consequence-bearing deployments whose failure can materially affect rights, safety, access, livelihood, public infrastructure, institutional authority, or durable public trust. It is not proposed as a universal licensing regime for every programmer or ordinary application.
nonClaims: Existing law already recognizes a Software Engineer of Record role.
One certification package can replace domain regulation, engineering standards, security review, or professional judgment.
Completion of paperwork proves that a deployment is safe or socially legitimate.

practicePrograms.title: Technical Leadership & Outside-Witness Consulting
practicePrograms.thesis: Technical leadership protects the conditions of closure; consulting helps teams see boundaries and failure modes that local process has normalized.

practicePrograms.title: Reliability, Security & Operational Repair
practicePrograms.thesis: A software system has not closed merely because it deployed; it must preserve its invariants through observation, attack, failure, recovery, change, and retirement.
topics: Fault containment, circuit breakers, bulkheads, sagas, outbox, retry, idempotency, and state machines
practicePrograms.claimBoundary: A synthesis and application framework grounded in established reliability, security, DevOps, SRE, accessibility, and safety practices; not a replacement for those fields or standards.

consultingPosture: Help teams make hidden boundaries, invariants, lifecycle states, authority gaps, and failure modes explicit enough that useful delivery can resume.

safeClaims: The lane extends and recontextualizes established software-engineering practice.
The methods can be evaluated through worked cases, decision changes, delivery outcomes, and independent practitioner use.
Patterns and architectures should be judged by the invariants and failure boundaries they preserve.
prohibitedClaims: Boundary First Labs invented Agile, Kanban, Domain-Driven Design, Clean Architecture, Onion Architecture, or the software patterns it interprets.
Every established method is merely a special case of Boundary First in a way that erases historical and technical differences.
The method is universally superior without comparative evidence.
Every programmer should be licensed or every software project requires the same professional controls.

history.orientation: This lane extends the established history of software engineering rather than claiming a replacement foundation. It places Agile, Kanban, requirements, architecture, patterns, reliability, maintenance, and technical leadership into a common account of observation, boundaries, invariants, flow, consequence, and repair.

historicalArc.development: The late 1960s and 1970s established software engineering as a response to scale, complexity, reliability, and project failure.

historicalArc.period: Objects, patterns, architecture, and domain modeling
historicalArc.development: Information hiding, objects, architectural styles, patterns, and domain-driven design supplied reusable ways to organize change and responsibility.

historicalArc.period: Agile, Lean, DevOps, and reliability practice
historicalArc.development: Iterative delivery, flow, continuous integration, operations, observability, and incident learning moved software toward continuous empirical stewardship.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: Closure-Driven Software Development reinterpreted delivery as the stabilization of useful form under uncertainty.

Agile was reframed as an observational system; Kanban as visibility into flow and blockage; patterns as boundary moves; and architecture as nested regimes of knowledge, ownership, exposure, refusal, and failure.
The lane then expanded into consequence-bearing software practice, technical leadership, consulting, accountability instruments, and reliability and repair.
aimsToward: Field guides and comparative literature maps that make the reinterpretation useful without erasing established practice.
Consulting and training that produce decision changes, bounded artifacts, and measurable delivery or reliability outcomes.
A scoped accountability stack for high-consequence software, including invariant declarations, deployment attestations, named responsibility, and repair protocols.

label: AI as Forge
short: Human-led AI for disciplined research and production.
title: AI is a forge, not an oracle.
body: Boundary First Labs uses generative AI as an assistive transformation instrument for search, comparison, extraction, drafting, coding, critique, and artifact production. AI as Forge governs the posture of use: provenance, claim discipline, bounded authority, visible uncertainty, and named human responsibility. It is distinct from Corpus Forge, the tool-independent research-operations protocol, and from the Computational & Machine Intelligence research program, which studies learning and representation technically. AI assistance does not confer authorship, legitimacy, independent review, or release authority.
takeaways: The human remains the smith.
Amplification requires review.
Agency cannot be outsourced.
No agent may grant itself authority.
claims: Generative AI may accelerate disciplined transformation without becoming the source of provenance, legitimacy, or release authority.
Material AI assistance should remain attributable where relevant, while named humans or institutions retain consequential responsibility.
AI as Forge is a use doctrine; Corpus Forge is the separate research-operations protocol.

label: Corpus Forge
short: A tool-independent protocol for provenance, criticism, adjudication, promotion, supersession, and preservation.
title: Make every consequential transformation inspectable.
body: Corpus Forge is the research-operations protocol used to move source material through stabilization, atomic extraction, claim and contradiction registration, independent criticism, human-scoped adjudication, stable-file mutation, promotion, supersession, and preservation. Its current vertical slice passes structural lineage and authority-separation checks and has a Critic-ready manuscript. Those checks establish inspectability and structural reproducibility, not semantic adequacy, legitimate human review, lower burden, scalability, truth, or a solution to AI accountability. Corpus Forge is tool-independent and distinct from AI as Forge, the general corpus, and epistemic authority itself.
takeaways: Provenance identifies origin; it does not validate a claim.
A declaration bounds authority; it does not manufacture authority.
Structural checks do not establish semantic adequacy.
A conventional workflow may absorb the entire profile.
Independent human review requires a named reviewer and attributable report.
claims: Corpus Forge presently constitutes an authority-bearing coordination profile over established provenance, research-object, version-control, and documentation mechanisms.
One retrospective vertical slice is structurally reproducible and internally adversarially tested.
Nonredundant value, lower burden, scalability, meaningful human review, and independent validation remain unproved.

label: Governance & Institutions
short: Authority, decision, representation, accountability, institutional stewardship, and repair.
title: Power must remain answerable to consequence.
body: This lane applies Representational Mechanics and Constructive Humanist Agentics to organizations, governance, law, economics, professional responsibility, public infrastructure, and the lab's own stewardship obligations. It studies who can act, who authorizes action, what evidence and classifications guide decisions, what boundaries and invariants must be preserved, who bears consequences, who can contest an outcome, and who possesses both the authority and capacity to repair failure. Boundary First Labs applies the same questions to its own claim governance, AI use, publication sequencing, conflicts, partnerships, and custody of consequential knowledge.
takeaways: Responsibility must remain traceable and capable of repair.
Bound authority and expose its consequence chain.
Participation without standing or recourse is not representation.
Institutional memory must support revision, replacement, and repair.
Apply the lab's governance principles to the lab itself.
Delegated authority requires standing, review, and a lawful route to repair.
A governance structure is incomplete when it can authorize construction but cannot assign maintenance and retirement.
claims: Institutional transparency is insufficient without contestability, accountable authority, and a viable repair path.
Concentrated power becomes functionally sovereign when meaningful exit, contest, and public accountability disappear.
Research institutions require explicit governance for provenance, claim maturity, publication, conflicts, review, and continuity.
Responsibility is incomplete when its holder lacks the authority, resources, or procedure required to repair failure.
coreThesis: Governance should keep authority, representation, provenance, responsibility, consequence, contestability, and repair structurally coupled—including within the institutions producing the research.

softwareAccountabilityInterface.principle: Consequential software authority should terminate in named human and institutional responsibility with standing, evidence, escalation, rollback, and repair.
softwareAccountabilityInterface.scopeBoundary: Controls scale with consequence and do not imply identical governance for every software system.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Boundary governance must itself be bounded
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: No institution should possess unreviewable authority to define who counts, what evidence matters, what consequences are visible, or when a dispute is closed.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Delegation must remain traceable
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: Authority should be transportable only through declared roles, purposes, scopes, durations, evidence rules, and revocation or escalation conditions.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Standing should track exposure to consequence
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: People and communities materially affected by institutional action require more than observation. They require a defined route to evidence, objection, appeal, and repair.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Institutional memory is accountability infrastructure
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: Decisions, evidence, dissent, exceptions, incidents, and repairs should remain legible across personnel changes and time.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Responsibility must include repair capacity
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: An office or role is not meaningfully responsible when it lacks the authority, resources, procedure, or information required to correct the failure assigned to it.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Plural institutions correct different boundary failures
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: Democracy, due process, science, adversarial review, independent courts, journalism, civic participation, local knowledge, and public-interest institutions provide distinct mechanisms for challenging defective representations and concentrated power.

institutionalDesignPrinciples.title: Maintenance should precede emergency repair
institutionalDesignPrinciples.body: Institutions should make lifecycle obligations, deferred defects, resource constraints, and handoff risks visible before accumulated failure becomes crisis.

programs.description: Maps the institution, cycle, pressure, decision boundaries, authority chain, affected agents, excluded consequences, contestability, memory, and repair capacity.
programs.claimCeiling: Diagnostic and design method; effects require pilot evidence.

programs.title: Public Agency and Delegated Authority
programs.description: Studies how public, corporate, professional, and artificial authority is granted, transported, bounded, revoked, and made answerable to affected people.
programs.claimCeiling: Institutional doctrine requiring legal and historical comparison.

programs.title: Governance as Repair Architecture
programs.description: Treats notice, evidence, appeal, audit, oversight, correction, compensation, redesign, and institutional learning as an integrated repair system.
programs.claimCeiling: Design framework requiring casework and comparison with established governance practice.

programs.title: Public Reason and Boundary Correction
programs.description: Examines how plural evidence channels, journalism, science, courts, public records, criticism, and civic participation make public boundaries contestable and correctable.
programs.claimCeiling: Public philosophy and institutional synthesis requiring literature and case support.

programs.title: Institutional Memory and Provenance
programs.description: Builds decision, evidence, exception, dissent, incident, maintenance, and repair records that survive personnel and organizational change.
programs.claimCeiling: Design program; privacy and legal retention obligations remain context-specific.

programs.title: Mission-Locked Public-Interest Laboratory
programs.description: Develops how Boundary First Labs and similar institutes can preserve independence, mission, claim discipline, criticism, public benefit, continuity, and financial sustainability.
programs.claimCeiling: Proposed institutional architecture pending legal and organizational implementation.

programs.title: Participation, Standing, and Local Knowledge
programs.description: Studies when consultation becomes meaningful representation, how local knowledge enters decisions, and what procedural power affected participants require.
programs.claimCeiling: Normative and design program requiring domain-specific public-process evidence.

institutePolicyInterface.principle: The laboratory should demonstrate internally the bounded authority, funding independence, criticism, evidence, privacy, maintenance, and repair duties it recommends publicly.
auditQuestions: Who owns this decision and who may reverse it?
What evidence and conflicts are visible?
Who bears consequences and has standing to object?
What funding or partnership pressure may distort judgment?
What record will survive the current decision makers?

history.orientation: The governance lane builds from constitutionalism, public administration, democratic theory, institutional economics, cybernetics, organizational sociology, and commons governance. Its central historical problem is how authority can act at scale without becoming unbounded, opaque, or unrepairable.

historicalArc.development: Authority was bounded through divided powers, law, representation, public office, and rights of challenge.
Large institutions developed procedures, records, expertise, and administrative capacity, while also creating new risks of opacity and displaced responsibility.
Scholars studied polycentricity, commons, public reason, organizational learning, and the role of local knowledge in legitimate coordination.

buildsFrom.author: Montesquieu
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for divided power and institutional checks.

buildsFrom.author: James Madison
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for structuring institutions so power checks power.

buildsFrom.author: Max Weber
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for bureaucracy, authority, office, and the rationalization of institutional power.

buildsFrom.author: John Dewey
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for publics constituted by shared consequences and governance as collective inquiry.

buildsFrom.author: Elinor Ostrom
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for polycentric governance, local knowledge, monitoring, graduated response, and durable commons institutions.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The lab reframed governance around who may act, who authorized the action, who bears the consequence, who can contest it, and who can repair failure.
Institutional doctrine expanded from AI governance into public agency, memory, provenance, standing, and mission-locked public-interest structures.
Governance was recast as a repair architecture rather than only a decision architecture.
aimsToward: Institutional Boundary Audits and public-agency maps that expose hidden authority and consequence chains.
Governance systems with durable memory, independent appeal, affected-party standing, and named repair capacity.
A formally adopted governance charter for Boundary First Labs that demonstrates the doctrine internally.

label: Law, Constitutional Systems & Public Trust
short: Delegated authority, standing, liability, contestability, and repair.
title: Law gives consequence an address.
body: This lane studies law as a representational architecture for admissible authority, public trust, rights, standing, evidence, liability, contestability, and repair. It asks who may act, under what authorization, which boundaries constrain that action, who may challenge it, how consequence is attributed, and which person or institution possesses both the duty and capacity to correct failure. The work spans constitutional structure, administrative process, antitrust and anti-sovereignty, corporate and artificial agency, tort and product responsibility, public-benefit entities, due process, appeals, and bounded public-trust architectures. It is a legal research and design program, not legal advice, and requires jurisdiction-specific sources and qualified review.
takeaways: No authority without authorization, boundary, contestability, and repair.
Public trust is a structural obligation, not a branding claim.
Private power becomes sovereignty-like when it controls agency-critical interfaces without meaningful exit, appeal, or public accountability.
Legal personhood must not become a sink in which human responsibility disappears.
Every legal claim must declare jurisdiction, source, posture, and review status.
claims: Law can be analyzed as a system for representing and transporting authority, evidence, consequence, liability, and repair across people and institutions.
Antitrust has a public-agency function when concentrated private control determines the conditions under which people and institutions may act.
Contestability, standing, appeal, and repair are not procedural ornaments; they are mechanisms by which defective authority can be detected and corrected.
A bounded public-trust architecture can be assembled from existing entity, covenant, fiduciary, contract, audit, and governance mechanisms, but implementation is jurisdiction-specific.
Artificial and corporate agents may exercise operational capacity without becoming self-authorizing or absorbing the responsibility of their human and legal stewards.

programs.description: Maps the chain from public purpose and delegated authority to duty, representation, consequence, oversight, and repair.
programs.claimCeiling: General institutional framework; legal meaning varies by jurisdiction and doctrine.

programs.title: Due Process, Contestability & Repair Rights
programs.description: Treats notice, reasons, standing, objection, appeal, remedy, reversal, and compensation as repair structures for consequential decisions.
programs.claimCeiling: Design and comparative analysis; not a declaration of specific legal entitlements absent authority.

programs.title: Corporate and Artificial Agency
programs.description: Examines how corporations, automated systems, committees, and AI agents exercise operational capacity while responsibility, authorization, and liability remain attributable.
programs.claimCeiling: Interpretive and policy research; no claim that current doctrine already adopts the framework.

programs.title: Tort, Product & Professional Responsibility
programs.description: Connects foreseeable consequence, product design, professional duty, organizational responsibility, and repair capacity across software and AI systems.
programs.claimCeiling: Research agenda requiring legal scholarship and qualified review.

programs.title: Purpose-Locked & Bounded Public-Trust Entities
programs.description: Explores combinations of PBCs, cooperatives, nonprofits, LLCs, trusts, SPVs, covenants, fiduciary duties, capped capital, audit, and reversion mechanisms.
programs.claimCeiling: Design pattern; entity choice and enforceability require counsel in each jurisdiction.

programs.title: Consequence-Bearing Software Accountability
programs.type: professional responsibility and institutional design research
programs.description: Examines invariant declarations, deployment attestations, responsible-charge roles, accountability chains, evidence packages, incident duties, liability, and repair for high-consequence software.
programs.claimCeiling: A design and comparative-law research program. No claim that a Software Engineer of Record role is presently recognized or appropriate in every jurisdiction or domain.

programs.title: Public Agency Doctrine
programs.description: Connects authorization, standing, reasons, refusal, appeal, responsibility, and repair so public power remains derivative from accountable institutions and answerable to affected people.
programs.claimCeiling: Normative and comparative legal program, not a statement of current law in every jurisdiction.

validationGates: Jurisdiction and legal posture declared
Primary and secondary legal sources
Distinction between description, critique, interpretation, and proposal
Qualified legal review before implementation
Conflict with existing rights, duties, remedies, and entity law assessed
Non-legal-advice disclosure
prohibitedClaims: The framework is binding law or legal advice.
Current doctrine already recognizes every proposed category.
A bounded public-trust structure is enforceable without jurisdiction-specific drafting.
Antitrust alone resolves every form of private power or institutional failure.
coreThesis: Law should keep delegated power, public consequence, standing, liability, contestability, and repair structurally connected.

questions: When does software consequence justify a named responsible-charge role?
What duties can be defined by contract, policy, professional standard, regulation, or statute?
What standing and remedies should affected people retain?
How should responsibility be distributed among engineers, executives, vendors, deployers, operators, and public authorities?
What evidence, attestation, and incident records are discoverable or auditable?

boundaryGovernanceSafeguards.principle: No hidden priesthood of boundary definers. Boundary governance must itself be bounded.
safeguards: Access to relevant evidence subject to legitimate privacy and security limits
Meaningful standing for materially affected parties
Public or auditable record of decisions and exceptions
Revocation, correction, compensation, and repair mechanisms
Protection against self-authorization and conflict capture
Periodic review of whether the authority remains necessary and legitimate
boundaryGovernanceSafeguards.essentialSystemsRule: Where exit is not realistic because a system is essential, monopolistic, legally compulsory, or infrastructural, procedural standing and repair obligations should become stronger rather than weaker.
boundaryGovernanceSafeguards.claimCeiling: Institutional and legal-design doctrine; implementation depends on jurisdiction, constitutional order, and domain.

history.orientation: The law lane builds from constitutional limitation, the rule of law, public trust, fiduciary duty, administrative due process, tort, corporate law, antitrust, and professional responsibility. It studies law as a formal representation of admissible authority and consequence.

historicalArc.development: Public office, common goods, jurisdiction, and the limits of rulers developed through layered legal and civic traditions.
Rights, due process, fiduciary obligations, tort, contract, corporate personhood, and public administration organized authority and responsibility.
Antitrust, product liability, administrative review, platform regulation, privacy, and AI accountability responded to new forms of concentrated and automated power.

buildsFrom.author: Lon L. Fuller

buildsFrom.author: Philip Selznick
buildsFrom.relation: Institutional and legal lineage for responsibility, integrity, and responsive institutions.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The corpus developed antitrust as anti-sovereignty law, public-agency doctrine, bounded authority, consequence-bearing software responsibility, and purpose-locked institutional forms.
Law was separated from general governance so jurisdiction, precedent, legal status, and professional review could receive their own claim gates.
The current lane treats legal proposals as design and research programs, not legal advice or claims of already-recognized legal forms.
aimsToward: Legal architectures that make authority, standing, evidence, appeal, liability, and repair explicit in consequential systems.
A bounded public-trust corporation or adjacent lawful structure capable of mission lock, stewardship, and public accountability.
Jurisdiction-specific analysis and expert review before any legal instrument is represented as deployable.

label: Finance, Capital & Economic Systems
short: Bounded capital, repair finance, household continuity, and economic consequence.
title: Finance is the law of who may borrow from the future.
body: This lane studies finance as a representational and institutional system for allocating present power against future labor, capacity, maintenance, ecology, and agency. It develops diagnostics and instruments that distinguish repayability from system-worthiness, reward durable value and repair capacity, expose propagated and externalized costs, and keep capital bounded by the future it creates. Boundary-Weighted Finance supplies the diagnostic framework. Repair Note Finance, the Boundary Trust architecture, the Living Systems Covenant, bounded-return capital, consequence covenants, repair reserves, platform-floor investment, barter and mutual-credit systems, and household-closure analysis form an emerging instrument portfolio. These are proposed architectures requiring calibration, legal design, professional review, and real-world pilots.
takeaways: Creditworthiness is not system-worthiness.
The more public the failure, the stricter the leverage boundary.
Finance should represent lifecycle cost, repair capacity, consent, propagation, opacity, and externality.
Capital must remain bounded by the future it creates.
Do not invent an economic invariant to justify a token, ledger, or financial product.
claims: Boundary-Weighted Finance is a diagnostic framework for distinguishing finance by durable value, repair capacity, consent, platform effect, propagation, externality, and opacity.
A financial representation is defective when it can bind or extract from a real system while excluding the maintenance, survival, or repair conditions by which that system must redeem the claim.
Repair Note Finance is an emerging mission-locked, bounded-return, outcome-audited financing architecture rather than a proven security, legal category, or calibrated asset class.
The Boundary Trust is an abstract institutional stack that may be implemented through existing legal forms rather than a claim to a newly recognized corporate form.
Household continuity, labor capacity, public infrastructure, and ecological substrate are economically material even when conventional ledgers place them outside the transaction boundary.

documents.title: Boundary Trust and Living Systems Covenant

programs.title: Boundary-Weighted Finance
programs.description: Scores or compares finance by durable value, repair capacity, consent, platform multiplier, propagation, externality, and opacity rather than repayment alone.
programs.claimCeiling: Diagnostic framework; not a calibrated underwriting formula or investment recommendation.

programs.title: Repair Note Finance
programs.status: emerging; concept stabilized in chat-derived work
programs.description: A mission-locked, bounded-return, outcome-audited financing instrument intended to fund repair, public capacity, and living-system continuity.
programs.claimCeiling: Instrument proposal requiring securities, tax, banking, entity, and contract review before offering or implementation.

programs.title: Boundary Trust / Bounded Public Trust Architecture
programs.description: An abstract stack of entity, purpose lock, bounded capital, consequence covenant, and independent audit. It may use a corporation, PBC, cooperative, nonprofit, LLC, trust, SPV, or combination of existing forms.
programs.claimCeiling: Institutional design pattern; not a claim that a new legal entity already exists or is available in every jurisdiction.

programs.title: Living Systems Covenant
programs.description: Declares protected human, ecological, institutional, and maintenance conditions that financed activity must preserve, measure, and repair.
programs.claimCeiling: Governance proposal pending legal drafting, measurable obligations, enforcement design, and pilot evidence.

programs.title: Platform-Floor Investment
programs.description: Evaluates investment by durable yield, household resilience, system repair, and expanded option space against build, maintenance, transition, and externalized costs.
programs.claimCeiling: Comparative heuristic pending calibrated metrics.

programs.title: Household Closure & Coherent-Wage Economics
programs.description: Studies whether wages, schedules, housing, care, health, transport, and risk permit households to sustain participation, planning, and repair.
programs.claimCeiling: Research and public doctrine pending empirical specification and comparison with labor, welfare, and household-economics literature.

programs.title: Barter, Mutual Credit & Capacity Exchange
programs.description: Matches underused goods, time, skills, tools, space, and institutional capacity to represented need, with accounting chosen to preserve reciprocity, trust, and repair.
programs.claimCeiling: Product and institutional experiment; no claim of replacing money, markets, banking, or public benefits.

programs.title: Public Credit & Future Agency
programs.description: Extends founding debates over public credit, monopoly, faction, and republican continuity into the question of whether finance may bind the future without representing the future.
programs.claimCeiling: Interpretive political economy requiring historical and legal sourcing.

validationGates: Legal and jurisdictional review
Securities, tax, banking, fiduciary, and contract analysis as applicable
Metric and proxy calibration
Conflict and incentive analysis
Outcome-audit design
Failure, default, wind-down, and repair terms
Pilot evidence and independent review
prohibitedClaims: Repair Notes are currently registered, approved, insured, or legally available.
Boundary-Weighted Finance is a validated investment or underwriting model.
The Boundary Trust is already a recognized universal corporate form.
A token or blockchain creates public value by itself.
The framework provides individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.
coreThesis: Finance should be judged by the future capacity, consequence, and repair obligations it creates—not repayment alone.

history.orientation: The finance lane builds from accounting, political economy, banking, corporate finance, public finance, institutional economics, financial instability, ecological economics, and impact-oriented capital. Its central question is what future conditions a financial claim creates or consumes.

historicalArc.development: Double-entry accounting, markets, credit, and public finance made obligations and ownership portable across time and institutions.
Corporate finance, banking, monetary theory, leverage, and public investment became central to large-scale production and instability.
Externalities, systemic risk, common goods, climate finance, impact measurement, and mission-locked enterprise broadened evaluation beyond private return.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: Economic critique moved from throughput and underutilization toward explicit analysis of leverage, repair capacity, externality, opacity, consent, and platform value.
Repair Note Finance, Boundary Trust, bounded-capital architecture, consequence covenants, and outcome audits were organized as an instrument stack rather than announced as established products.
The barter and capacity-exchange work created a practical lane for representing underused resources, needs, trust, and reciprocal value.
aimsToward: Financial instruments whose obligations include maintenance, repair, public consequence, and the future agency they enable or constrain.
Qualitative casebooks and empirical calibration before quantitative scores are treated as validated measures.
Lawfully implementable mission-locked structures that can attract capital without allowing capital to silently redefine the public purpose.

label: Infrastructure & Civilizational Repair
short: Maintenance ownership, lifecycle cost, repair capacity, and civilizational continuity.
title: Construction is incomplete until maintenance and repair have a home.
body: This lane studies infrastructure as a lifecycle obligation rather than a construction event. It develops public doctrine, models, casework, software, and institutional designs for naming the people, offices, funding paths, records, inspections, repair authority, and retirement conditions required to preserve operational closure over time. Civilizational Tech Debt names the unpaid closure costs hidden when visible progress displaces maintenance, risk, repair, or survival burden into another representation. Maintenance Agent of Record, Lifecycle Closure Cost, No Orphan Assets, No Unfunded Delegation, shared consequence ledgers, and public-works transparency provide the initial constructive program.
takeaways: Infrastructure without a named maintenance agent is delayed failure.
Build cost is not lifecycle cost.
No agent may create or benefit from infrastructure while displacing its lifecycle obligation into an unrepresented future.
Maintenance, repair, replacement, and retirement belong inside the initial design and funding boundary.
Public transparency becomes useful when it links assets, condition, ownership, money, consequence, and repair.
claims: Civilizational tech debt names unpaid closure costs displaced into maintenance, repair, risk, ecological burden, or survival burden while another representation records apparent efficiency or progress.
A Maintenance Agent of Record is the named role, office, institution, or contractual structure responsible for preserving an infrastructure system after construction.
Lifecycle Closure Cost includes construction, operation, inspection, maintenance, repair, replacement, transition, and retirement obligations rather than capital expenditure alone.
Orphan assets and unfunded delegation are structural failure modes because authority to create consequence has been separated from responsibility and capacity to maintain or repair it.
Software, datasets, models, and digital public systems carry infrastructure obligations when institutions and people depend upon their continued operation.

caseStudyTemplate: What asset or service is being sustained?
Who is the Maintenance Agent of Record?
What operating, inspection, maintenance, repair, replacement, and retirement obligations exist?
What records make condition and consequence legible?
What defects are currently displaced or deferred?
Who can halt, repair, transfer, or retire the system?
What happens if the steward or funding path disappears?
coreThesis: A consequence-bearing system is not complete until stewardship, lifecycle funding, maintenance, failure, repair, transfer, and retirement have accountable homes.

civilizationSystems.title: Civilization-Scale Systems
civilizationSystems.claimStatus: systems-theoretic synthesis and research program; not a complete mathematical theory of civilization or a solution to the Great Filter
civilizationSystems.stackPrinciple: Each layer depends on lower layers and constrains upper layers. Modern agency amplifiers couple the layers tightly enough that local defects can propagate into domains that did not authorize or represent the original action.
agencyAmplifiers: biotechnology and direct intervention in living systems

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Agency amplification
boundaryFilterSequence.question: What new capacity to perceive, decide, coordinate, produce, persuade, or act has been created?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Boundary stress
boundaryFilterSequence.question: Which human, legal, social, epistemic, ecological, material, or temporal boundary is placed under new pressure?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Representational exclusion
boundaryFilterSequence.question: Which people, dependencies, costs, uncertainties, or future effects fall outside the dominant metric or decision frame?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Local defect accumulation
boundaryFilterSequence.question: What harm, debt, fragility, dependency, distortion, or loss accumulates while the system appears locally successful?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Defect percolation
boundaryFilterSequence.question: How can the local defect connect to finance, law, ecology, knowledge, health, infrastructure, legitimacy, conflict, or future agency?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Closure test
boundaryFilterSequence.question: Can the civilization still detect, contest, fund, coordinate, and execute repair before connected failure becomes effectively irreversible?

boundaryFilterSequence.title: Repair or filter failure
boundaryFilterSequence.question: Does the system internalize the boundary as law, redesign the amplifier, and restore capacity, or does it automate and normalize the violation?

civilizationAudit: What agency amplifier is being created or scaled?
What local objective or metric is the system optimizing?
Which human, social, legal, epistemic, ecological, material, or temporal boundary is stressed?
What harm or dependency lies outside the dominant representation?
How could the defect propagate across connected systems?
Can affected agents understand, challenge, refuse, exit, appeal, or repair the change?
Who answers if the system fails?
What material substrate is consumed, degraded, or made dependent?
What options are removed from future agents?
Should the system be allowed, bounded, certified, taxed, slowed, localized, redesigned, prohibited, dismantled, or placed under stronger stewardship?
failureDomains: security, conflict, biological, and catastrophic risk
safePublicClaims: Civilization can be studied as a stack of coupled social, technical, institutional, and material systems.
Powerful technologies can propagate consequences across domains that were absent from the local objective.
Maintenance, contestability, public knowledge, accountability, and repair capacity are relevant to civilizational resilience.
The Boundary Filter Hypothesis is a diagnostic and research frame rather than a settled scientific result.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim to have solved the Fermi paradox or identified the single Great Filter.
Do not claim that collapse is inevitable or that all boundaries are good.
Do not claim that boundary language replaces climate science, economics, law, biosecurity, nuclear strategy, AI safety, or other domain disciplines.
Do not claim a mathematically proved universal law of civilizations without formal and empirical support.
Do not use civilization-scale diagnosis as a license for unaccountable centralized control.

history.orientation: The infrastructure lane builds from public works, maintenance engineering, systems ecology, reliability and resilience engineering, risk studies, infrastructure studies, and long-term stewardship. It emphasizes that construction is only the beginning of an asset’s consequence chain.

historicalArc.period: Ancient and early modern public works
historicalArc.development: Roads, water systems, fortifications, ports, and civic works demonstrated that collective capacity depends on maintenance, administration, and intergenerational stewardship.
Large technical systems joined engineering, finance, bureaucracy, standards, and public risk.
Scholars studied normal accidents, ecological resilience, invisible maintenance labor, network interdependence, and cascading failure.

buildsFrom.author: Lewis Mumford
buildsFrom.relation: Historical and critical lineage for technology as an institutional and civilizational system.

buildsFrom.author: C. S. Holling
buildsFrom.work: Resilience and Stability of Ecological Systems
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for resilience, regime change, and the difference between stability and adaptive persistence.

buildsFrom.author: Charles Perrow
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for systemic risk in tightly coupled complex systems.

buildsFrom.author: Susan Leigh Star and Karen Ruhleder
buildsFrom.work: Steps Toward an Ecology of Infrastructure
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for infrastructure as relational, embedded, learned, and often visible only upon breakdown.

buildsFrom.author: Donella H. Meadows et al.
buildsFrom.relation: Civilizational systems lineage for feedback, resource limits, delay, and overshoot.

buildsFrom.author: Bent Flyvbjerg, Nils Bruzelius, and Werner Rothengatter
buildsFrom.relation: Lineage for accountability, forecasting failure, and risk in large infrastructure programs.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: Civilizational Tech Debt generalized deferred maintenance and displaced closure cost across software, public works, institutions, ecology, and future generations.
Maintenance Agent of Record, Lifecycle Closure Cost, No Orphan Assets, and No Unfunded Delegation turned diagnosis into institutional design rules.

The civilization stack and Boundary Filter work extended infrastructure reasoning into coupled systems of personhood, family, culture, economy, law, state, science, technology, ecology, and future agency.
aimsToward: Concrete case studies that connect asset condition, funding, authority, affected publics, failure propagation, and repair ownership.
Infrastructure governance in which every consequential asset has a named steward, lifecycle budget, evidence record, and lawful retirement path.
Civilization-scale diagnostics that remain explicitly bounded as systems research rather than claims to predict history with certainty.

label: Systems Criticism & Public Diagnosis
short: Casework, critique, red teams, counterarguments, and repair-oriented criticism.
title: Criticism detects the defect a system has learned not to see.
body: This lane organizes the lab’s large body of critique and criticism as a disciplined public practice rather than a residual category. It applies boundary-first analysis to finance, markets, law, politics, software, AI, media, education, professional norms, organizations, infrastructure, labor, ecology, and academic research. It also turns the same machinery inward through red teams, publication-risk audits, counterarguments, limitations, corrections, and public responses. Satire may make a defect vivid, but this lane carries the evidence, comparison, causal caution, and repair proposal required for serious criticism.
takeaways: Criticism is institutional maintenance.
Diagnose the representation, boundary, incentive, and displaced consequence—not only the visible failure.
Critique becomes constructive when it identifies a repair path, comparison, or test.
Apply the same standards to Boundary First Labs that the lab applies to external systems.
Satire may reveal a contradiction; evidence must carry the claim.
claims: Many persistent public failures remain stable because the representation used to evaluate the system excludes the people, costs, timescales, or maintenance burdens that would reveal the defect.
Criticism can be made more accountable by declaring its target, evidence, causal posture, alternatives, affected parties, and proposed repair path.
A research institution requires an explicit criticism loop so that provenance, coherence, or founder authority cannot harden into insulation from correction.
Casework is a bridge between public doctrine and formal theory because it reveals where the grammar succeeds, overreaches, or fails to distinguish important mechanisms.

programs.title: Boundary Failure Casebook
programs.description: Indexes failures by pressure, representation, excluded boundary, protected invariant, displaced consequence, closure defect, responsibility, and repair path.
programs.claimCeiling: Case-specific diagnosis; cross-case generalization requires comparative evidence.

programs.title: Economic & Finance Critique
programs.description: Covers value extraction, leverage, public credit, monopoly, K-shaped outcomes, externality laundering, household closure, and the separation of accounting from accountability.
programs.claimCeiling: Interpretive and empirical claims require data and literature; rhetoric does not establish causality.

programs.title: Institutional & Political Critique
programs.description: Examines representation, delegated authority, public trust, accountability gaps, faction, institutional opacity, and consequence without standing.
programs.claimCeiling: Public argument and comparative institutional analysis; jurisdiction-specific assertions require sources.

programs.title: Technology, AI & Software Critique
programs.description: Critiques throughput-first development, authority laundering through AI, hidden failure, premature abstraction, unowned maintenance, and systems that amplify action faster than accountability.
programs.claimCeiling: Technical doctrine and casework; empirical performance claims require benchmarks.

programs.title: Academic & Professional Critique
programs.description: Examines credentialing, disciplinary fragmentation, claim inflation, publication incentives, professional responsibility, and the difference between learning a discipline and constructing one.
programs.claimCeiling: Interpretive critique requiring institutional comparison and care against overgeneralization.

programs.title: Boundary First Labs Red Team
programs.description: Publishes objections, claim ceilings, failed tests, unresolved conflicts, alternative explanations, and changes made in response to criticism.
programs.claimCeiling: Governance commitment; credibility depends on documented practice and external participation.

critiqueTemplate: What system and claim are being criticized?
What representation does the system use to evaluate itself?
Who or what lies outside that representation?
What consequence is displaced, delayed, or rendered illegible?
What alternative explanations or counterarguments remain?
What repair, test, comparison, or institutional change is proposed?
What would falsify or materially revise the criticism?
claimFirewall: Criticism may identify contradictions, incentives, exclusions, and likely failure paths. It does not establish motive, causality, illegality, or universal generalization without the evidence appropriate to those claims.
coreThesis: Criticism is a repair discipline for exposing excluded consequence, testing public claims, and preventing institutions from becoming insulated from their own defects.

publicDiagnosisStandard.principle: Critique should make hidden consequence legible without pretending that a common grammar erases domain differences.
requiredElements: What would falsify or materially revise the diagnosis
publicFormats: satirical performance paired with a sourced analytic companion
publicDiagnosisStandard.repairRule: A criticism need not contain a complete solution, but it should identify the missing boundary, responsible institution, evidence gap, or experiment required for repair whenever that can be done safely.

history.orientation: The criticism lane builds from Socratic examination, philosophical critique, political economy, genealogy, ideology critique, pragmatist inquiry, systems analysis, investigative journalism, safety analysis, and red-team practice. Its task is to make normalized defects visible and answerable.

historicalArc.development: Questioning, disputation, and public argument tested claims, habits, and authority.
Political economy, sociology, genealogy, and critical theory examined how institutions produce categories, power, and concealed consequence.
Safety engineering, incident review, adversarial testing, investigative reporting, and technology criticism exposed coupled failures and design assumptions.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: Critique emerged throughout the corpus as economic, institutional, software, AI, academic, and civilizational diagnosis.
The lane was separated from satire so sourced analysis, causal confidence, counterarguments, and repair proposals could receive explicit standards.
Internal red teams and correction ledgers made criticism a maintenance function of the lab rather than merely an outward-facing posture.
aimsToward: A Boundary Failure Casebook grounded in evidence, counterarguments, claim status, and repair options.
A public culture in which criticism remains connected to correction rather than becoming detached performance or partisan identity.
Regular red-team and response practices that expose defects in the lab’s own work before public authority accumulates around them.

label: Software, Products & Testbeds
short: Platforms, public utilities, professional tools, technical assets, pilots, and demonstrations.
title: Build public value; let reality answer.
body: Boundary First Labs maintains a diversified software and product portfolio that translates research into public value, constructive coordination, professional practice, measurable evidence, distribution, and sustainable income. The portfolio ranges from large constructive-media and civic-economic platforms to small human-centered mobile utilities, research and governance workbenches, licensable technical assets, and domain testbeds. Products are not treated as unrelated app ideas: they share a concern with preserving knowledge, coordinating constructive action, maintaining human agency, exposing hidden system state, and connecting failure to repair. Large platforms express the lab's long-range institutional vision; smaller utilities and professional tools create near-term value and force the research into contact with use.
takeaways: Build useful systems at multiple scales.
Treat products as translations of shared research, not disconnected ideas.
Select the smallest credible wedge that preserves the larger invariant.
Measure public value, operational failure, and income potential separately.
Let product defects refine the theory, methods, and portfolio sequence.
Treat financial, legal, and institutional architectures as testable instruments with professional review gates.
A public-interest product includes its maintenance, funding, contestability, and retirement conditions.
No product without a named steward, maintenance path, and retirement condition.
Human factors, accessibility, reliability, privacy, and security belong inside the product definition.
claims: The software portfolio is a diversified translation layer between foundational research and public use.
Large platforms can express long-range institutional vision while bounded utilities and professional tools produce near-term value, evidence, distribution, and revenue.
A product belongs in the portfolio when it preserves knowledge, coordinates constructive action, maintains human agency, exposes hidden system state, or connects failure to repair.
A method becomes more credible when independent users can repeat it and expose its failure modes.
Products are research instruments when their defects feed back into definitions, models, governance, and design rules.
coreThesis: The software portfolio turns the lab's research into public value, constructive infrastructure, professional practice, measurable evidence, distribution, and sustainable institutional capacity.
portfolioThesis: Boundary First Labs builds software that helps people preserve knowledge, coordinate constructive action, maintain human agency, expose hidden system state, and connect failure to repair.
economicThesis: Large platforms express the lab's long-range institutional vision; small utilities, professional tools, and technical assets create near-term public value, evidence, distribution, and sustainable income.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Create real public value
portfolioPrinciples.body: A project should solve a recognizable problem, improve access or agency, preserve useful knowledge, or strengthen public and institutional capacity.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Begin with a bounded wedge
portfolioPrinciples.body: Do not build the entire platform before a small product has demonstrated the relevant users, constraints, invariants, and failure modes.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Preserve the shared research architecture
portfolioPrinciples.body: Projects may ship independently, but their public descriptions should show how they relate to representation, admissibility, agency, consequence, continuity, and repair.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Keep maturity visible
portfolioPrinciples.body: Confirmed, emerging, and candidate projects must not be presented as though they possess equal provenance, implementation, or market readiness.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Use revenue to extend the mission
portfolioPrinciples.body: Income potential is a legitimate design constraint when it supports institutional continuity without displacing the public-interest purpose of the work.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Return use to research
portfolioPrinciples.body: Product use, defects, support burdens, user behavior, and failed assumptions should update the lab's theories, methods, and portfolio priorities.

portfolioPrinciples.title: No product without a steward
portfolioPrinciples.body: Every active product, testbed, dataset, or instrument must name who maintains it, how incidents are handled, how maintenance is funded, and what happens when stewardship ends.

portfolioPrinciples.title: Design for real human operation
portfolioPrinciples.body: Human factors, accessibility, privacy, security, reliability, and support must be treated as product boundaries rather than late-stage polish.

portfolioStatusLegend.meaning: Founder-originated concept, architecture, workflow, implementation, manuscript, or product direction that belongs to the current Boundary First Labs asset inventory. Confirmed does not imply market-ready.
Supported by existing work and current direction, but still requires sharper product definition, architectural selection, or pilot evidence.
Strongly aligned with the portfolio but not yet established as an active founder-originated asset; retained in the incubator rather than presented publicly as mature work.

softwarePortfolio.title: Projectr
softwarePortfolio.productType: constructive media network and structured knowledge platform
softwarePortfolio.description: A constructive media network for creating, sharing, revising, and coordinating projects, plans, goals, procedures, learning paths, evidence, progress, and reusable public knowledge. Its primary objects are constructive and revisable rather than disposable posts.
publicValue: Turns attention into structured agency and reusable knowledge.
Supports collaborative planning, learning, documentation, and public problem solving.
Creates a durable home for constructive media rather than engagement-only media.
incomePotential: Subscriptions for advanced workspaces and organizational use.
Creator, education, community, and enterprise tooling.

softwarePortfolio.title: YouTube Knowledge Explorer
softwarePortfolio.productType: learning wrapper and educational media tool
softwarePortfolio.description: A learning layer over YouTube that turns playlists, channels, and selected videos into structured learning paths with notes, dependencies, progress, summaries, and explicit reasons for what to watch next.
publicValue: Converts video feeds into navigable learning environments.
Helps teachers, creators, families, and independent learners organize durable knowledge.
Provides an accessible on-ramp into the larger Projectr ecosystem.

softwarePortfolio.title: Cross-Platform Bookshelf
softwarePortfolio.productType: personal knowledge and media organizer
softwarePortfolio.description: A structured bookshelf for videos, articles, podcasts, books, documents, and courses that preserves why an item was saved, where it belongs, the user's intended use, progress, relationships, and resulting knowledge or action.
publicValue: Preserves learning intent instead of merely accumulating links.
Connects media consumption to projects, goals, and action.
Reduces fragmentation across platforms and formats.

softwarePortfolio.title: Constructive Media Protocol
softwarePortfolio.productType: constructive knowledge and media infrastructure
softwarePortfolio.description: A protocol layer for identifying, attributing, versioning, relating, transporting, forking, correcting, rewarding, and preserving constructive media and public knowledge across systems.
publicValue: Makes constructive knowledge portable, composable, and correctable.
Preserves attribution, lineage, and revision across platform boundaries.
Provides infrastructure for durable public knowledge rather than isolated content silos.

softwarePortfolio.title: Barter and Capacity Exchange
softwarePortfolio.productType: civic-economic exchange network
softwarePortfolio.description: A structured exchange network for matching underused goods, services, time, tools, space, transport, care, expertise, inventory, and productive capacity to represented human and organizational need.
publicValue: Makes underused capacity and unmet need mutually legible.
Supports exchange where conventional money is absent, scarce, or an incomplete representation of value.
Creates public-interest infrastructure for neighborhoods, mutual-aid groups, nonprofits, and small organizations.
incomePotential: Transaction, matching, or administrative service fees where appropriate.
Municipal, nonprofit, cooperative, and community deployments.

softwarePortfolio.title: Barter Ledger
softwarePortfolio.productType: accounting, provenance, credit, and settlement layer
softwarePortfolio.description: A durable accounting layer for exchange, reciprocal obligation, contribution, portable reputation, mutual credit, and settlement. Blockchain is treated as one possible implementation rather than the product's purpose.
publicValue: Creates legible and durable exchange records.
Supports trust, reciprocity, and contribution accounting across communities.
Allows the ledger architecture to be selected by the invariants of the exchange system.
softwarePortfolio.designConstraint: Choose the ledger that preserves the economic invariant; do not invent an economic invariant to justify the ledger.

softwarePortfolio.title: Need and Capacity Map
softwarePortfolio.productType: public-interest matching and coordination tool
softwarePortfolio.description: A bounded tool for representing underused resources, unmet needs, matching constraints, and trusted organizations capable of closing the gap before attempting to build a complete alternative economic system.
publicValue: Provides immediate coordination value without requiring a new currency.
Supports neighborhood, nonprofit, school, disaster-response, and mutual-aid use.
Generates evidence about what a larger exchange system must preserve.
incomePotential: Integration with resource-management and civic systems.

softwarePortfolio.title: Child-Safe Video Calling
softwarePortfolio.productType: bounded mobile communication utility
softwarePortfolio.description: A video-call environment that allows a caregiver to hand a young child a live call without exposing the rest of the phone or allowing random touches to hang up, change settings, open applications, send messages, or make purchases.
publicValue: Preserves safe family connection for children too young to operate a general-purpose phone.
Demonstrates safety through explicit negative capability and bounded interaction.
Creates an accessible consumer example of boundary-first interface design.
incomePotential: Partnerships with communication, accessibility, and family-service providers.
softwarePortfolio.designConstraint: The child receives the intended human connection while irrelevant operational control remains inaccessible.

softwarePortfolio.title: Family Presence Mode
softwarePortfolio.productType: caregiver-mediated communication and accessibility environment
softwarePortfolio.description: A reduced and trusted communication environment for children, elderly users, people with cognitive or motor impairments, hospitalized family members, and others who need human connection without general-device complexity.
publicValue: Expands safe communication beyond the child-use case.
Preserves human presence while removing irrelevant operational complexity.
Supports accessibility, caregiving, and remote family connection.
incomePotential: Licensed communication modes for device or platform providers.

softwarePortfolio.title: Single-Purpose Phone Modes
softwarePortfolio.productType: bounded mobile interaction framework
softwarePortfolio.description: A framework for temporarily turning a general-purpose phone into a bounded appliance for one trusted activity, such as emergency contact, medical instruction, school pickup, elder check-in, navigation, appointments, tickets, or household tasks.
publicValue: Reduces accidental action, confusion, distraction, and misuse.
Creates accessible interfaces for users who do not need the full device surface.
Provides a reusable architecture for a family of small public-value applications.

softwarePortfolio.title: Corpus Forge
softwarePortfolio.productType: research operations and corpus stewardship workbench
softwarePortfolio.stage: operational internal workflow moving toward product
softwarePortfolio.description: A workbench for turning notes, documents, conversations, models, and experiments into a traceable, versioned research system through ingestion, source preservation, claim extraction, artifact classification, contradiction tracking, maturity control, provenance, review gates, and replacement documents.

Score confirmed and emerging projects by public value, founder leverage, implementation cost, time to evidence, time to revenue, and strategic composability.

researchRelationship: The software portfolio and computational research portfolio are connected but not interchangeable. Computational research produces theories, primitives, architectures, experiments, constraints, and negative results. Products selectively embody that work, test it against public use, and return evidence, failure cases, and revenue to the lab.
scientificResearchRelationship: Mathematics and physics contribute theorem targets, numerical experiments, simulations, and domain testbeds. Products may embody selected results, but no product inherits mathematical proof or physical validity merely by implementing a research idea.
softwarePracticeRelationship: The product portfolio tests and monetizes selected software-engineering methods. Software Engineering & Applied Computer Science governs delivery, architecture, technical leadership, maintenance, and consulting practice; this node records the actual products, platforms, utilities, workbenches, pilots, and technical assets built under those disciplines.

portfolioLifecycle.title: Portfolio Lifecycle & Stewardship
portfolioLifecycle.principle: The lab applies its own no-orphan-assets rule to every product, instrument, dataset, service, and public commitment.

lifecycle.label: Seed
lifecycle.description: A sourced idea or need with no commitment that it will become a product.

lifecycle.label: Governed Concept
lifecycle.description: Purpose, users, boundaries, public value, risks, and claim ceiling are declared.

lifecycle.label: Bounded Prototype
lifecycle.description: The smallest implementation capable of exposing real use and failure.

lifecycle.label: Testbed
lifecycle.description: A controlled environment for gathering evidence and revising the concept.

lifecycle.label: Pilot
lifecycle.description: A named external user or partner operates the system under bounded conditions.

lifecycle.label: Product or Instrument
lifecycle.description: A maintained public, professional, institutional, or licensed offering.

lifecycle.label: Maintained Service
lifecycle.description: Ongoing support, security, updates, governance, funding, and evidence collection exist.

lifecycle.label: Retirement, Transfer, or Open Release
lifecycle.description: Stewardship ends through a declared migration, archive, transfer, open release, or shutdown.

portfolioLifecycle.application: Every public project record should identify its current lifecycle stage and may not be presented as a maintained product until support, security, funding, ownership, and retirement conditions exist.

history.orientation: The product and testbed lane follows traditions of experimental apparatus, prototypes, design science, pilot programs, living labs, open-source development, and industrial research. Its purpose is to force ideas into contact with users, materials, organizations, and failure.

historicalArc.development: Instruments and apparatus made theories answerable to repeatable observation.
Models, pilots, and iterative prototypes allowed technical and social systems to be tested before full deployment.

historicalArc.period: Design science, open source, and living labs
historicalArc.development: Artifacts became research outputs whose usefulness, adoption, maintenance, and community modification could provide evidence.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The software inventory was organized into platforms, public utilities, professional tools, technical assets and testbeds, and incubator concepts.
Each asset was given a maturity state, public-value thesis, income potential, evidence path, maintenance obligation, and sunset condition.
Products were positioned as both public offerings and instruments through which the research can fail visibly and improve.
aimsToward: A balanced portfolio in which small utilities create immediate value while larger platforms express the institutional vision.
A governed route from seed to prototype, pilot, maintained product, transfer, or retirement.
External use and revenue that strengthen independent research capacity without silently redefining the mission.
history.citationNote: Representative lineage, not a claim of derivation or equivalence. Before publication, verify editions, translations, page references, and the exact relation of each citation to the local claim.

label: On-Ramps & Education
short: Examples, diagrams, glossaries, workshops, and teaching systems.
title: Multiple doors into the same research.
body: The on-ramp lane turns abstract mechanics into ordinary questions, familiar examples, visual explanations, workshops, public talks, satire, and domain-specific teaching tools. Checklists, bug reports, contracts, game boards, dashboards, household routines, chess positions, comic monologues, and mock-philosophical dialogues help readers encounter pressure, cycle, grammar, distinction, boundary, admissibility, closure, defect, invariant, consequence, and repair before specialized terminology becomes necessary. The theory may be new; the questions are ancient; the method is the bridge.
takeaways: Start from a familiar recurring failure.
Teach the mechanism before the name.
Use ordinary questions as the public interface.
Keep metaphor and formal claim distinct.
Let performance open the door while the underlying argument remains inspectable.
Satire may reveal a defect; it does not by itself establish the diagnosis.
claims: Boundary-first practice can give ordinary judgment a repeatable and increasingly rigorous procedure.
The observable cycle is often the most concrete entry point to the operative system.
coreThesis: Ordinary examples and questions provide accessible interfaces to deep representational structure.
scientificOnRamps: Field, flow, weather, and spectral visualizations
Claim-maturity guides separating proof from physical evidence
evidenceOnRamps: How mathematical and physical evidence differ
How a prototype becomes a maintained product
How criticism, correction, and replication change the corpus
How to participate in a pilot or review

history.orientation: The education lane builds from dialogue, demonstration, visual pedagogy, progressive education, constructivism, apprenticeship, popular science, critical pedagogy, and constructionism. It teaches mechanisms through familiar problems before requiring specialized vocabulary.

historicalArc.development: Learning occurred through questioning, imitation, practice, and guided participation.
Educators emphasized observation, activity, development, and learning through consequences rather than recitation alone.
Learners were treated as builders of models and artifacts, with diagrams, manipulatives, simulations, and programmable media supporting understanding.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The public on-ramp work began with ordinary examples—checklists, bugs, contracts, games, dashboards, and familiar failures.
Boundary-First Chess, MapReduce interpretations, classical geometry, visual essays, and glossaries became domain-specific entrances into the same mechanics.
The lane adopted a rule to teach the mechanism before the name and to keep metaphor, historical explanation, and formal claim distinct.
aimsToward: A layered curriculum from intuitive examples to methods, formal foundations, and domain practice.
Workshops and public media that let people test one useful instrument without accepting the entire research program.
Accessible educational systems that preserve human factors, disability access, multiple modes of explanation, and transparent claim status.

label: Public Philosophy & Satire
short: Talks, satire, mock-Greek philosophy, and cultural critique.
title: Serious ideas need a public voice.
body: This lane carries Boundary First Labs into rooms where formal papers, software methods, and institutional prose cannot go by themselves. It uses public speaking, satirical monologue, mock-Greek dialogue, pseudo-symposium, philosophical performance, story, and cultural critique to expose contradictions, test intuitions, teach representational mechanics, and make difficult ideas memorable. The Carlin Lane supplies the sharper comedic and cultural-critical voice. Mock-Greek philosophy supplies a playful classical frame for staging arguments, rival schools, category errors, and absurd institutional logics. These forms are substantive public-intellectual work, but not an evidentiary shortcut: rhetoric may reveal the shape of a problem while the supporting research remains independently inspectable.
takeaways: Comedy can expose a hidden boundary before a definition can name it.
Satire is a diagnostic and pedagogical instrument, not a proof.
Let the joke open the door; let the argument carry the weight.
Make serious ideas memorable without trivializing their consequences.
A public philosophy should survive questions from the room.
claims: Public philosophy is an intake surface through which audiences can encounter, test, and contest difficult ideas before entering formal machinery.
Satire can make contradictions, excluded consequences, false closures, and institutional evasions perceptible by rendering them difficult to ignore.
Performance provides live evidence about legibility, confusion, resistance, and which representations survive transport into ordinary language.
Mock-philosophical forms can compare rival positions and expose category errors while remaining explicitly fictional and non-authoritative.

coreThesis: Public speaking, satire, and philosophical performance make consequential ideas memorable and contestable while preserving a clear boundary between rhetoric and validation.

history.orientation: This lane builds from Socratic dialogue, Cynic performance, Menippean satire, public oratory, pamphleteering, literary satire, stand-up comedy, and philosophical lecture. It uses humor and staged argument to make hidden assumptions visible without treating rhetoric as evidence.

historicalArc.development: Socratic questioning, Aristophanic comedy, Cynic performance, and later dialogues made philosophy public, adversarial, embodied, and memorable.
Satire became a vehicle for criticizing institutions, dogma, hierarchy, war, and economic absurdity.
Public intellectual performance and comedy created mass forms for social diagnosis outside academic institutions.

boundaryFirstDevelopment: The corpus developed a Carlin Lane, mock-Greek schools and figures, satirical dialogues, monologues, and lecture-performance forms.
The lane was separated from general criticism and education so performance could preserve its own voice and craft.
A claim firewall was added: satire may diagnose, illustrate, provoke, and teach, but does not independently validate formal, empirical, or historical claims.
aimsToward: A recognizable public-speaking and performance tradition for Boundary First Labs.
Paired formats in which satire creates access and a sourced analytic companion supplies evidence and claim boundaries.
Live and recorded work capable of bringing institutional, economic, technological, and philosophical critique to wider publics.
